src/java.base/share/classes/java/securit.short_description: PEM encoder for various DER-encoded security objects, with optional PBE encryption for private keys.
src/java.base/share/classes/java/securit.description:
PEMEncoder is a library-class in java.security that converts DER-encoded cryptographic objects into PEM textual encodings. It centralizes logic for producing PEM blocks for certificates, CRLs, public keys, private keys, PKCS#8 encoded keys, EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo, KeyPair (OneAsymmetricKey), and application-specific PEMRecord objects. The class exposes both byte[] and String outputs and provides a withEncryption(char[]) configuration method to obtain an encoder instance that will encrypt private keys using the JVM-configured default PBE algorithm.

This class is designed to be immutable and thread-safe: the default singleton instance PEM_ENCODER is stateless (no password), while withEncryption(...) returns a new PEMEncoder instance that initially stores a PBEKeySpec. The actual SecretKey is derived lazily and cached when first needed (inside buildKey), and a ReentrantLock serializes secret-key generation to avoid redundant SecretKeyFactory invocations. PEMEncoder maps many low-level exceptions to IllegalArgumentException to present a consistent API surface to callers. It relies on internal Sun classes (sun.security.util.Pem, sun.security.pkcs.PKCS8Key, sun.security.util.DerOutputStream, sun.security.x509.AlgorithmId) to perform the low-level encoding and to construct OneAsymmetricKey and encrypted PKCS#8 representations.

Because PEMEncoder interacts with algorithm selection via the security property jdk.epkcs8.defaultAlgorithm and uses provider Cipher/SecretKeyFactory in conjunction with AlgorithmParameters, edits must respect the existing lazy initialization, locking, exception mapping, and the restricted supported input types. The implementation enforces semantic rules (for example: only PrivateKey may be encrypted; certificates/CRLs/PEMRecord cannot be encrypted), and uses ISO_8859_1 for byte conversions of the produced PEM string. The class is annotated as a preview API (PreviewFeature.PEM_API) and is expected to be part of public API surface for callers in JDK 25+.

src/java.desktop/unix/classes/sun/font/N.short_description: Maps Unicode code units to native font glyph indices using an X11 encoding mapper
src/java.desktop/unix/classes/sun/font/N.description:
NativeGlyphMapper is a small, platform-specific implementation of the CharToGlyphMapper abstraction used by the JDK font subsystem. It exists to translate Unicode code units (char or int code points) into glyph indices understood by a NativeFont instance on Unix/X11 platforms, delegating the translation work to an XMap instance that represents the font's encoding. The class stores a reference to the NativeFont, uses XMap.getXMapper(font.encoding) to obtain a per-encoding converter, caches the number of glyphs from the NativeFont, and sets the missing glyph index to 0.

The design separates concerns: NativeGlyphMapper binds a particular NativeFont to an XMap translation table while CharToGlyphMapper (the superclass) defines the API used by text layout and rendering code. This class is intentionally small and efficient: its mapping functions are simple array lookups against xmapper.convertedGlyphs, implemented for single-code-unit and array-based conversions as well as an NS (non-subsituting) variant that currently delegates to the normal conversion. Because NativeGlyphMapper relies solely on the XMap conversion tables (an array of int glyph indices), it does not attempt to determine whether a code point is actually present in the font beyond what the encoding mapping provides — a limitation noted in the file comments and reflected in the design.

Interactions: NativeGlyphMapper is tightly coupled to NativeFont (for numGlyphs and encoding) and to XMap (for convertedGlyphs and encoding-specific mapping). It is used by higher-level font/text layout code (classes that expect a CharToGlyphMapper implementation) when rendering or measuring text with a NativeFont on Unix platforms. The class assumes that XMap and NativeFont provide consistent data; edits should respect that contract and the expectations of the CharToGlyphMapper API.

src/java.desktop/share/classes/sun/font/.short_description: Utility class with platform flags and Unicode/font-layout helpers used by the JDK font subsystem
src/java.desktop/share/classes/sun/font/.description:
FontUtilities is an internal sun.font utility class that centralizes platform detection, logging control and text-layout / glyph-mapping helper routines used across the JDK font stack (Swing, Java2D, font managers and text layout code). It exists to provide a single authoritative place for: determining platform booleans (isLinux, isMacOSX, isWindows, isMacOSX14, useJDKScaler), providing access to the Font2D representation for java.awt.Font, exposing logging helpers, and encapsulating logic that decides whether sequences of characters require complex shaping/layout or can be treated as simple left-to-right 1:1 char->glyph mappings.

The file contains a static initializer that queries OSInfo and system properties to set runtime flags; these flags affect font scaler selection and logging behavior. It also defines constants (MIN_LAYOUT_CHARCODE, MAX_LAYOUT_CHARCODE) used by text layout code to decide when shaping may be necessary and implements several predicate helpers: isComplexCharCode (int codepoint), isNonSimpleChar (char), isComplexText/isComplexScript (char[] ranges), isDefaultIgnorable (codepoint table-based check aligned with HarfBuzz's default-ignorable list), and isIgnorableWhitespace. These helpers encode unicode-range tables and special-case logic (ZWJ/ZWNJ, directional controls, combining diacritics, Indic scripts, Tibetan, Khmer, Thai, etc.) and must be kept consistent with other shaping libraries and expectations of text rendering code.

FontUtilities also provides Swing-oriented helpers, notably fontSupportsDefaultEncoding() and getCompositeFontUIResource(Font), and maintains a SoftReference cache (compMapRef) mapping PhysicalFont to CompositeFont to support creating composite FontUIResources that behave like system composite fonts. The class is internal to the JDK and interacts closely with Font2D, FontAccess, FontManagerFactory / FontManager, CompositeFont, PhysicalFont, and CharToGlyphMapper; changes to signature/semantics here will impact many consumers in the font rendering pipeline. Because of this, edits must respect platform detection semantics, logging initialization, concurrency and caching behavior (SoftReference + volatile), Unicode range tables, and the difference between APIs that take 'char' (may contain surrogates) vs. 'int' codepoints (actual Unicode code points).

src/java.base/aix/classes/sun/nio/fs/Aix.short_description: AIX-specific FileSystemProvider implementing file store and user-defined attribute view support
src/java.base/aix/classes/sun/nio/fs/Aix.description:
This class provides the AIX-specific implementation of the internal FileSystemProvider used by the JDK's sun.nio.fs package. It extends the UnixFileSystemProvider abstraction to supply AIX-tailored FileSystem, FileStore and FileAttributeView behaviors. The file exists to encapsulate platform differences for AIX (IBM AIX OS), such as whether a FileStore supports the user-defined ("user") attribute view and to construct AIX-specific implementations (AixFileSystem, AixFileStore, AixUserDefinedFileAttributeView) where appropriate.

Design decisions: AixFileSystemProvider delegates generic Unix behavior to its superclass (UnixFileSystemProvider) while overriding a small set of platform-specific operations: creation of AixFileSystem instances, creation/lookup of AixFileStore objects for paths, and exposing the UserDefinedFileAttributeView only if the underlying FileStore advertises support for it. The class implements a helper supportsUserDefinedFileAttributeView(UnixPath) which queries the FileStore capability, intentionally swallowing IOExceptions and treating any failure as 'unsupported' (returns false). The two getFileAttributeView entry points (typed and dynamic-by-name) create and return AixUserDefinedFileAttributeView instances only when the FileStore indicates support, otherwise they return null and otherwise defer to the UnixFileSystemProvider implementation.

How it fits into the system: this file is part of the platform-specific subset of java.base (the AIX implementation). It interacts directly with AixFileSystem and AixFileStore classes and with the UnixPath abstraction and Util helpers. Changes here affect how Files.getFileAttributeView and Files.getFileStore behave on AIX and therefore can alter the observable Files API behavior on that platform. The commit history indicates a past bug where the provider unconditionally returned a view even when the FileStore did not support the user-defined attributes; this class now ensures compliance with the Files API contract by returning null when unsupported.

insights.title: Return null from getFileAttributeView when UserDefinedFileAttributeView unsupported
insights.problem: Files.getFileAttributeView returned an implementation even when the underlying FileStore did not support UserDefinedFileAttributeView, producing unusable views and potential user confusion/crashes.
insights.root_cause: AixFileSystemProvider unconditionally returned a new AixUserDefinedFileAttributeView without checking store capability, and supportsUserDefinedFileAttributeView used a Path parameter named obj incorrectly in some variants.
insights.solution: Added supportsUserDefinedFileAttributeView that queries Files.getFileStore and updated getFileAttributeView and getFileAttributeView(name) to first check support and return null if unsupported. Also reorganized code to create UnixPath once and pass it to the view constructor.
insights.lesson_learned: When providing platform-specific attribute views, always check FileStore capabilities before returning a view; returning a non-functional view violates the Files API contract.

This file is the package-level Javadoc for the jdk.jfr package (Java Flight Recorder API). src/java.base/share/classes/java/nio/fil.short_description: Factory and accessors for default and non-default FileSystem instances using FileSystemProviders
src/java.base/share/classes/java/nio/fil.description:
This class is the central factory and accessor for FileSystem instances in the JDK. It implements the public static API that user code calls to obtain the default FileSystem (getDefault) and to locate or construct other FileSystem instances identified by URI or Path (getFileSystem, newFileSystem overloads). The class mediates between client requests and concrete implementations of java.nio.file.spi.FileSystemProvider, using the system-installed providers (FileSystemProvider.installedProviders()) and, optionally, service loading via a supplied ClassLoader.

Key design decisions visible in this file: lazy initialization of the default FileSystem via the nested static DefaultFileSystemHolder class; special-casing of startup via VM.isModuleSystemInited so that during very early startup a platform default filesystem is always used; support for an override property (java.nio.file.spi.DefaultFileSystemProvider) that chains or replaces the platform provider via reflective constructors; use of case-insensitive scheme matching; and deliberate swallowing of UnsupportedOperationException from providers when attempting to construct a filesystem so that other providers or loaders can be tried. The class also distinguishes between "installedProviders" (system classloader / platform fallback) and providers discovered via a ServiceLoader built from a caller-supplied ClassLoader.

This file interacts with internal and platform classes (jdk.internal.loader.ClassLoaders, jdk.internal.misc.VM, and sun.nio.fs.DefaultFileSystemProvider) and with the FileSystemProvider SPI and FileSystem/Path/URI public types. Changes here can affect boot-time behavior (startup ordering and module-system initialization), provider loading semantics, and how the default file system is created and returned to user code.

src/java.base/share/classes/jdk/internal.short_description: Precomputes and provides fast access to ASCII hex digit pairs for bytes (0–255).
src/java.base/share/classes/jdk/internal.description:
HexDigits is a small, focused utility in the java.base module that exists to provide a very fast primitive for converting single byte values (0–255) into two ASCII hexadecimal characters packed into a Java short. The class precomputes a 256-entry short[] table (DIGITS) where each element encodes the ASCII characters for the low and high nibble of a byte in little-endian order (low byte = ASCII of low nibble, high byte = ASCII of high nibble). This avoids per-call character arithmetic and branching when other parts of the JDK need to emit hex representations.

The design is deliberately low-level and micro-optimized: DIGITS is initialized once in a static initializer, annotated with @Stable so the JVM may treat it as stable for runtime optimizations. The public API is a single public static method digitPair(int i, boolean ucase) that masks the input to a byte range and returns the precomputed short, optionally adjusted to upper-case ASCII via a bitwise trick. The class is final with a private constructor because it is a pure utility holder and not meant to be instantiated or extended. It is intended to be used by other internal utilities that assemble hex strings or buffers efficiently and must be careful to respect the packing and case semantics implemented here.

It is annotated @Stable and created in a static initializer; its layout (low byte = low nibble ascii, high byte = high nibble ascii) and length must be preserved. Changes to its type, layout, initialization, or the @Stable annotation can affect correctness and JIT optimizations.

src/java.base/share/classes/jdk/internal.short_description: Annotation used by javac to mark API declarations as associated with a preview feature and carry JEP metadata.
src/java.base/share/classes/jdk/internal.description:
This source file declares an internal annotation type jdk.internal.javac.PreviewFeature that is used to mark API declarations (types, methods, fields, packages, modules, constructors) as associated with a preview language or VM feature. It exists to record, in compiled class files, that an API element belongs to a named preview feature and to carry small metadata (the feature key and whether reflective access is expected). This annotation is handled specially by the javac toolchain and tooling that generates symbol information and reads classes produced by other JDKs (see header comments which reference symbol generation and ClassReader code paths). The design intentionally uses RetentionPolicy.CLASS (not RUNTIME) and a constrained set of @Target values that match meaningful targets of java.lang.Deprecated (omitting local variables and parameters).

The annotation includes an inner enum Feature enumerating preview feature keys for the current release and an inner annotation JEP used to attach JEP metadata (number, title, status) to enum constants. The Feature enum contains feature constants with inline JEP annotations for some entries and explanatory comments indicating that some constants exist only to avoid warnings when building interim javac against an older boot JDK (i.e., constants may be retained temporarily to silence class-reading warnings). The file therefore plays a small but important role for backward/forward compatibility of compiler toolchains and produced class files when features are in preview across JDK releases.

Because this annotation is interpreted by build-time tooling and class-reading code, any edits must respect compatibility constraints: its retention and target choices, the exact enum constants used (names and presence), and the way JEP metadata is attached. The header comment explicitly names two other components that coordinate with this source: CreateSymbols.java (symbol generation when producing older-release stubs) and com.sun.tools.javac.jvm.ClassReader (class-reading logic). Changes here may require corresponding changes in those files and will affect how --release older-release works and whether the compiler or tooling emits warnings when loading classes referencing preview features.

src/java.base/share/classes/jdk/internal.short_description: Produces plain-text or JSON thread dumps to files or byte arrays for VM diagnostics
src/java.base/share/classes/jdk/internal.description:
This class is the Java-side implementation used by the VM to implement the Thread.dump_to_file diagnostic command and the HotSpotDiagnosticMXBean.dumpThreads API. It produces thread dumps (plain text or a simple formatted JSON) and can write the output to a file or return it as a UTF-8 encoded byte array. The class is placed in jdk.internal.vm because it is invoked directly by the VM and HotSpot diagnostic plumbing rather than being a general-purpose utility.

ThreadDumper orchestrates collecting thread snapshots (via ThreadSnapshot.of) and container hierarchy information (via ThreadContainers.root()) and then serializes that information in two formats. It centralizes the logic for file handling (create vs create-new semantics when overwrite is disallowed), error reporting to the tool user (returns small UTF-8 encoded messages when file creation fails), and bounding of byte-array returns (MAX_BYTE_ARRAY_SIZE and a BoundedByteArrayOutputStream). The class carefully converts runtime and per-thread metadata (process id, Instant.now, Runtime.version, thread id/name/state, stack frames, monitored locks, park blockers, carrier threads for virtual threads) into the chosen output format.

Design choices visible in the file: (1) multiple public entry points matching VM/DX API needs: dumpThreads(String, boolean) and dumpThreadsToJson(String, boolean) for diagnostic commands, plus stream-based overloads (OutputStream) for HotSpotDiagnosticMXBean; (2) a minimal JSON serializer (nested JsonWriter) rather than using a full JSON library, to keep dependencies small and deterministic in formatting; (3) explicit handling of I/O via TextWriter and UncheckedIOException wrapping to convert checked IOExceptions to unchecked while serializing and then rethrowing the original cause to the API callers that expect checked exceptions; (4) defensive handling when ThreadSnapshot.of returns null (snapshot unavailable/terminated): the dumpThread methods return boolean to indicate whether a thread was actually serialized so callers can correctly compute threadCount.

Interactions and dependencies: ThreadDumper depends on several VM-specific helper types not present in this file: ThreadSnapshot, ThreadContainer / ThreadContainers, TextWriter, BoundedByteArrayOutputStream, and uses Objects.toIdentityString for object identity. The VM will call the string-based overloads; other Java code (HotSpotDiagnosticMXBean) will call the stream-based overloads. The JSON writer implements some JSON-specific behaviors (e.g., serializing Long as quoted string to avoid unsafe JSON integer ranges).

insights.title: Avoid dumping threads that have terminated during snapshot creation
insights.problem: ThreadDumper attempted to dump threads even if ThreadSnapshot.of returned null (e.g., thread terminated), causing access violations or misleading output.
insights.root_cause: ThreadSnapshot.of previously threw UnsupportedOperationException; after native change it can return null to signal snapshot couldn't be created. Dump code didn't handle null and proceeded.
insights.solution: ThreadDumper methods now handle null snapshots by returning a boolean indicating whether a dump was written; callers increment threadCount only when a dump occurred.
insights.lesson_learned: When API changes to return null for 'not available' instead of throwing, update consumers to handle the null case gracefully to avoid NPEs or spurious output.

src/java.base/share/classes/sun/nio/ch/N.short_description: NIO-based SocketImpl providing socket I/O, timeouts and virtual-thread aware non-blocking behavior
src/java.base/share/classes/sun/nio/ch/N.description:
NioSocketImpl is the java.net.SocketImpl implementation backed by native sockets and NIO primitives. It exists to provide the socket semantics used by java.net.Socket and ServerSocket while leveraging non-blocking I/O, temporary direct buffers and integration with the platform poller (including special handling for virtual threads). The class implements a small state machine for socket lifecycle (created, unconnected, connecting, connected, closing, closed) and manages both blocking and non-blocking modes so that legacy blocking semantics (timeouts, blocking threads) and newer virtual-thread semantics are preserved.

Key design decisions encoded in this file include: (1) explicit locking (readLock, writeLock) to serialize read/write operations and to coordinate state transitions; (2) a stateLock protecting socket lifecycle and thread fields (readerThread, writerThread); (3) switching sockets to non-blocking mode only when needed (timeouts or virtual threads) via configureNonBlockingIfNeeded, preserving initial blocking behavior; (4) use of temporary direct buffers (Util.getTemporaryDirectBuffer / Util.offerFirstTemporaryDirectBuffer) to perform native read/write syscalls without forcing large heap buffers; and (5) registering a Cleaner to ensure native FileDescriptor resources are closed if the Java object is collected.

NioSocketImpl interacts closely with the native and internal runtime pieces in sun.nio.ch: Net (socket creation and polling), IOUtil (configure blocking), Poller (virtual-thread poll path), NativeThread (native thread id bookkeeping), NativeDispatcher/SocketDispatcher (actual native read/write calls), and utility classes like Util, IOStatus and DirectBuffer. Correct behavior depends on careful coordination with those components and adherence to the documented locking/state rules in this class.

src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.short_description: KeyFactorySpi implementation for XDH (X25519/X448) keys; converts/generates Key and KeySpec forms.
src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.description:
This file implements a KeyFactorySpi for XDH (X25519 and X448) within the Sun security provider. It exists to translate between JCA Key instances, encoded forms (X.509/PKCS#8), and KeySpec implementations (XECPublicKeySpec/XECPrivateKeySpec), while enforcing algorithm parameter locking when this factory is constructed with a NamedParameterSpec. It is the piece of the provider that performs creation and normalization of XDH public/private key objects (XDHPublicKeyImpl and XDHPrivateKeyImpl), validates and maps formats, extracts encoded bytes, and ensures sensitive material (private scalars and encoded byte arrays) is cleared after use.

Design choices visible here include: use of XECParameters as the canonical representation of curve/parameter identity (the factory stores a lockedParams to enforce that the factory only operates on a single parameter set when constructed with a parameter spec), explicit handling of JCA encoding format strings "X.509" and "PKCS#8", and careful zeroing of temporary byte arrays (Arrays.fill) for private key material. The class centralizes exception mapping (InvalidKey -> InvalidKeySpec conversion), and uses Java language features (switch with pattern matching for types and records) to concisely dispatch KeySpec variants.

This class sits inside the provider implementation and interacts directly with other sun.security.ec classes: XECParameters (parameter canonicalization), XDHPrivateKeyImpl and XDHPublicKeyImpl (concrete key implementations and parsing constructors), and sun.security.pkcs.PKCS8Key (used when extracting embedded public keys from PKCS#8). Changes here affect how keys are parsed/validated and how keys produced by other provider components are accepted/translated by the KeyFactory. Because it handles sensitive material, it has security-sensitive behaviors (clearing byte arrays), exact-format comparisons, and must preserve interoperability with encoded key blobs from other implementations.

src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.short_description: Representation and parsing/encoding of PKCS#8 private keys (v1 and v2) with serialization support
src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.description:
PKCS8Key is a core JDK internal representation for PKCS#8 private keys. It exists to parse DER-encoded PKCS#8 (RFC 5958) structures into an object that holds algorithm identifier, private key material (as raw DER octet string), optional PKCS#8 attributes, and optional encoded public key for PKCS#8 v2. The class also produces canonical PKCS#8 encodings (caching the generated encoding) and provides integration points so that provider-specific PrivateKey implementations can be created from the parsed bytes (via KeyFactory) while preserving the ability to fall back to a raw PKCS8Key if the algorithm isn't supported by providers.

The design separates algorithm-independent handling (DER parsing, versioning, context-specific tags, caching encoded bytes, and secure memory handling) from algorithm-specific decoding which is left to subclasses or to KeyFactory when converting to concrete PrivateKey implementations. It supports both PKCS#8 v1 (version 0) and v2 (version 1) formats: v1 typically contains version, algorithmId, and privateKey octet string; v2 can also contain attributes (context tag 0) and an optional publicKey (context tag 1). The decode method conservatively parses these optional context-specific components and stores them in fields for later use in generateEncoding.

Security-sensitive behaviors are explicit: raw private key material (privKeyMaterial) and cached encodedKey are zeroed in clear(); getEncoded() returns a clone; getEncodedInternal() caches and returns an internal reference (synchronized) and is used by equals/hashCode for constant-time comparison via MessageDigest.isEqual. Serialization is handled defensively: writeReplace() returns a KeyRep(Type.PRIVATE) carrying algorithm, format, and the internal encoding; readObject handles legacy serialized PKCS8Key instances by decoding incoming DER from an ObjectInputStream (the class previously serialized itself instead of a KeyRep). The class integrates with internal JDK facilities (SharedSecrets.getJavaSecuritySpecAccess().clearEncodedKeySpec) to ensure intermediate sensitive buffers are cleared after use.

pitfalls.mistake: Replacing or removing the synchronized caching in getEncodedInternal or returning the internal array directly from getEncoded.
pitfalls.consequence: May introduce race conditions, expose internal mutable sensitive buffers to callers, or break semantics of equals/hashCode and serialization.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the synchronization and the defensive cloning semantics already present: keep getEncoded() returning a clone and getEncodedInternal() as the internal cached accessor.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering decode's handling of context-specific tags 0 and 1 or changing tag semantics.
pitfalls.consequence: Will break compatibility when parsing v1/v2 keys, causing InvalidKeyException on valid inputs or producing incorrect pubKeyEncoded/attributes values.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep exact parsing order and checks: sequence -> integer version -> AlgorithmId -> octet string privKeyMaterial -> optional [0] attributes -> optional [1] publicKey for v2.

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or changing the clearing behavior in clear() or the finally clearing of DerValue in decode.
pitfalls.consequence: Sensitive private key material may remain in memory, regressing security guarantees.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve calls to Arrays.fill on privKeyMaterial and encodedKey and DerValue.clear() calls where present.

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming getEncodedInternal never returns null (e.g., using it without checking after generateEncoding failure).
pitfalls.consequence: MessageDigest.isEqual or Arrays.hashCode with a null argument could throw NullPointerException or lead to unexpected behavior.
pitfalls.prevention: Treat getEncodedInternal as potentially null in new code paths unless you ensure generateEncoding cannot fail; existing code implicitly expects non-null but defensive checks are sensible if adding new callers.

src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.short_description: Provider KeyFactorySpi implementation for EC keys (translate/generate/validate EC keys).
src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.description:
This file implements a KeyFactorySpi for elliptic curve (EC) keys used by the SunEC provider. It exists to convert between generic Key/KeySpec/X.509/PKCS#8 encodings and the JDK's internal EC key implementations (ECPublicKeyImpl, ECPrivateKeyImpl), to validate EC keys, and to provide a static helper (toECKey) to obtain an ECKey instance suitable for use by other JDK subsystems (such as ECDSA/ECDH code). The implementation centralizes EC-related key conversion semantics (formats supported, how encoded bytes are interpreted, and how KeySpecs map to internal key objects) and is the authoritative place for these conversions within the SunEC provider.

Key design choices visible in the code: conversions accept both provider-neutral interfaces (ECPublicKey/ECPrivateKey) and encoded blobs (X.509 for public, PKCS#8 for private). The class uses internal implementation classes (ECPublicKeyImpl/ECPrivateKeyImpl) to produce keys that are expected by other SunEC components. It also takes care to zero-sensitive byte arrays (Arrays.fill) after processing encoded private key bytes. The implementation uses modern Java language features (pattern matching for instanceof and switch expressions), so any edits must preserve compatible Java language level and semantics. The class lazily acquires a KeyFactory instance for the SunEC provider via getInstance() and uses KeyFactory.translateKey in toECKey for converting keys that are not ECKey instances.

This file interacts closely with other Sun security classes: internal EC key implementations (ECPublicKeyImpl, ECPrivateKeyImpl), sun.security.pkcs.PKCS8Key (used to extract embedded public keys from PKCS#8 private key blobs), and the JCA KeyFactory/KeySpec APIs. It maps JCA constructs (X509EncodedKeySpec, PKCS8EncodedKeySpec, ECPublicKeySpec, ECPrivateKeySpec) to internal objects and enforces algorithm equality checks (exact string "EC").

src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.short_description: CertificateFactorySpi implementation for parsing, caching, and interning X.509 certs and CRLs
src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.description:
X509Factory is the Sun/Oracle provider implementation of java.security.cert.CertificateFactorySpi for X.509 v3 certificates, CertPaths, and X.509 v2 CRLs. It exists to parse certificate and CRL input streams (DER, PEM/base64, or PKCS#7 blobs), to produce X509CertImpl/X509CRLImpl instances and CertPath objects, and to provide an internal interning/caching layer so identical encoded certificates/CRLs map to shared in-memory representatives. The class centralizes parsing logic (including PEM handling and PKCS#7 detection), enforces an encoding size limit for caching, and converts general X509Certificate/X509CRL instances to the internal impl classes when needed.

Design choices visible in the file include (1) tight coupling with internal impl types (X509CertImpl, X509CRLImpl) so the factory can return optimized, interned objects rather than generic Certificate/CRL wrappers; (2) use of a soft-memory Cache to avoid pinning entries while enabling reuse; (3) careful InputStream handling via PushbackInputStream and readOneBlock semantics to allow mixed sequences of DER/PEM/PKCS#7 items; and (4) synchronization around cache access and the public intern(...) entry points to preserve thread-safety of cache lookups and inserts. The factory methods map to the standard CertificateFactorySpi engine* entry points (engineGenerateCertificate, engineGenerateCertificates, engineGenerateCRL, engineGenerateCRLs, engineGenerateCertPath, etc.) and translate I/O and parsing errors into the appropriate CertificateException/CRLException types expected by callers.

When making edits, be aware this class is system-critical for certificate parsing and is used widely by the security stack (truststores, TLS, CertPath building, etc.). It interacts with sun.security.x509.* impl classes, sun.security.pkcs.PKCS7, sun.security.util.Pem/DerValue utilities, and a shared Cache implementation. Changes to stream parsing, error semantics, returned object types, or cache behavior can have far-reaching compatibility and performance effects. The file contains protective limits and synchronization intended to prevent memory/DoS issues and ensure canonicalization of certificate objects; these semantics must be preserved or considered carefully when modifying behavior.

src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.short_description: Implements creation and verification of the TLS/SSL Finished handshake message across protocol versions.
src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.description:
This class encapsulates the logic for producing and consuming the Finished handshake message for multiple protocol versions (SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0/1.1, TLS 1.2, TLS 1.3). The Finished message is the cryptographic proof that both endpoints share the same handshake state and secrets; this file centralizes the different verify_data generation schemes and the handshake-level transitions that must happen when Finished is produced or received.

Finished.java is tightly integrated into the handshake state machine: it uses HandshakeContext (and its subclasses ClientHandshakeContext/ServerHandshakeContext), HandshakeHash, the negotiated CipherSuite (hash algorithms and lengths), ChangeCipherSpec handling, and session bookkeeping (including secure renegotiation and resumption). The file provides nested/inner classes to represent the Finished handshake message (FinishedMessage), the verify-data generation strategies for different protocol versions (VerifyDataScheme enum and version-specific VerifyDataGenerator implementations), and handshake producers/consumers to plug into the broader SSL/TLS handshake machinery.

Design choices visible in the file: version-specific generation is separated via a VerifyDataGenerator interface and a VerifyDataScheme enum to pick the generator based on negotiated protocol; cryptographic operations use provider APIs (KeyGenerator with TlsPrfParameterSpec for TLS 1.0/1.2, Mac/HMAC for TLS 1.3). The file also reflects security-sensitive care: derived secrets are handled with KeyUtil.destroySecretKeys in finally blocks (commit history shows migration to KDF APIs and extra care to avoid leaking raw key bytes). Error/alert conditions escalate using the handshake context's fatal(Alert, message, cause) pattern so failures produce appropriate TLS alerts.

pitfalls.mistake: Calling getEncoded() or otherwise exposing raw key material of derived SecretKey without ensuring the format is RAW or securely clearing bytes.
pitfalls.consequence: May leak sensitive key material into heap memory, or cause a ProviderException/incorrect behavior if non-RAW formats are returned.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect provider formats, use deriveData when available, and ensure derived SecretKey instances are destroyed (KeyUtil.destroySecretKeys) in finally blocks.

pitfalls.mistake: Not checking verify_data length and protocol-specific expectations when decoding a received Finished message.
pitfalls.consequence: Malformed Finished messages could be accepted or cause BufferUnderflow, leading to silent protocol breakage or incorrect Alert types.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the explicit verifyDataLen logic (36 for SSL30, 12 for <=TLS1.2 default, hash length for TLS1.3) and use context.conContext.fatal with appropriate Alerts on mismatch.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering handshake sequencing logic (e.g., updating consumers/producers or invoking ChangeCipherSpec) without reproducing existing ordering checks (EncryptedExtensions, Certificate, CertificateVerify comparisons).
pitfalls.consequence: Interoperability failures and subtle interop security issues where peers send messages in an unexpected order (commit history shows a bug where Finished processed early because EncryptedExtensions consumer entry remained).
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve state updates that register/unregister handshake consumers and producers and ensure explicit unexpected-message checks are kept consistent with other message handlers.

src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.short_description: KeyFactorySpi implementation for RSA/RSASSA-PSS: translate, validate and generate RSA keys and KeySpecs.
src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security.description:
This file implements a KeyFactory service provider for RSA-related algorithms (RSA and RSASSA-PSS) inside the Sun security provider. It exists to convert between generic JCA Key/KeySpec representations and the SunRsaSign internal RSA key implementations (RSAPublicKeyImpl, RSAPrivateKeyImpl, RSAPrivateCrtKeyImpl), to enforce key size/exponent constraints, and to provide utilities used by other RSA components in the JDK (e.g., RSASignature and RSACipher). The class centralizes RSA-specific policy (min/max modulus bit lengths, optional restricted exponent policy) and consistent handling of encoded key bytes, including wiping private key encodings after use.

Design-wise, RSAKeyFactory extends KeyFactorySpi and implements the JCA contract for engineTranslateKey/engineGenerate{Public,Private}/engineGetKeySpec. It delegates format-specific parsing and construction to RSAPublicKeyImpl/RSAPrivateCrtKeyImpl/RSAPrivateKeyImpl helper methods and to sun.security.pkcs.PKCS8Key when necessary. The class supports multiple KeyType variants (KeyType.RSA and KeyType.PSS) via a type field, and exposes small public helpers (toRSAKey, checkKeyLengths) used by other Sun providers. The implementation is defensive: it validates algorithm name matches, wraps other providers' misbehaving implementations with InvalidKeyException, constrains exponent length based on a system property, and zeroes out temporary byte[] encodings that may contain private key material.

As part of the JDK provider code, edits to this file affect low-level cryptographic semantics and compatibility. It must preserve public JCA behavior (format handling X.509/PKCS#1 for public keys and PKCS#8/PKCS#1 for private keys), existing exceptions/messages where external code may depend on them, and memory-cleanup patterns. The file uses recent Java language features (pattern matching in instanceof and switch with guarded patterns) consistent with the platform language level used in the repository.

insights.title: Avoid crash when verification expects DumpTimeClassInfo
insights.problem: Bytecode verification path assumed a DumpTimeClassInfo existed for non-shared classes; when classes were bulk-loaded earlier (AOT bulk loader) before dumptime table init, get_info() could be null and crash.
insights.root_cause: Classes can be loaded before dump mode is enabled (transitive AOT bulk-load during startup) so Klass::set_name didn't call init_dumptime_info. Later verification or add_verification_constraint assumed an entry existed.
insights.solution: Lazily create dumptime info entries for non-shared classes when needed (SystemDictionaryShared::init_dumptime_info called) before verification and constraint addition; also added defensive checks before using dumptime_table()

insights.title: Move class initialization to safe branch and handle exceptions during preload
insights.problem: During pre-linking/preloading, initialization errors (exceptions) could be unreported or propagated incorrectly.
insights.root_cause: initialize() was not invoked in the same control path where it should be, and pending exceptions weren't being turned into non-fatal warnings during preload/link-time operations.
insights.solution: Call ik->initialize(THREAD) in the else branch of try_link_class and convert any pending exception into a logged Preload Warning, clearing the exception so preload continues.

insights.title: Use hash set of newly loaded class names for deduplication
insights.problem: Deduplication loop used O(N*M) string comparisons leading to inefficiency for large archives/new classes.
insights.root_cause: Previously code did nested loops comparing archived and newly_loaded_classes by name.
insights.solution: Build a ResourceHashtable of newly loaded class names for O(1) membership checks during deduplication.

insights.title: Cap shared_classpath_index to avoid SIGSEGV when merging with shorter classpath
insights.problem: When the primary archive used more classpath entries than the merge run, shared_classpath_index could point past AOTClassLocationConfig length and later be dereferenced causing SIGSEGV.
insights.root_cause: class location indices from an archived primary cache were out-of-range for the new config during merge.
insights.solution: Cap out-of-range shared_classpath_index values to a safe fallback (app_cp_start_index or 0) when dumptime config length is smaller, logging the correction.

insights.title: Multi-cache merge helper flow and class extraction
insights.problem: Need to merge multiple AOT caches; archives cannot be mapped simultaneously so classes must be extracted from secondary caches.
insights.root_cause: Archives are fixed-address snapshots and the JVM lacks multi-archive lookup. Secondary archives required a helper to enumerate class names.
insights.solution: Implemented fork_extract_helper to spawn helper VMs that dump archived class names to temp files (dump_archived_classlist), then load those classes in main VM (load_and_link_classes_from_secondary_classlist), and orchestrated via extract_classes_from_secondary_caches during start_merging_aot_cache.

insights.title: Clear and handle pending exceptions during helper-driven class loading
insights.problem: resolve_or_null calls when loading classes from extracted lists can leave pending exceptions leading to unexpected aborts.
insights.root_cause: resolve_or_null can set a pending exception if resolution fails; merge flow must be tolerant and continue.
insights.solution: After resolve_or_null and try_link_class calls, check HAS_PENDING_EXCEPTION and CLEAR_PENDING_EXCEPTION, log and skip classes that fail to resolve/link.

insights.title: Prepare newly loaded classes for inclusion in merged AOT cache
insights.problem: When merging an existing AOT cache at VM shutdown, classes loaded at runtime may have refcounted symbols and missing classpath indices; such classes would not be correctly archived or matched in the merged cache.
insights.root_cause: Merge mode loads new classes at runtime (not during static dump) so their symbols might not be permanent and their shared_classpath_index can be unset (-1). Also archived input info (FileMapInfo) conflicts with creating new output unless freed.
insights.solution: Collect only newly-loaded classes for merging, assign shared_classpath_index based on loader type (boot/platform/app/custom), make class and CP symbols permanent, free input FileMapInfo when producing output, and ensure archived_method_handle_intrinsics pointer is nulled when merging.
insights.lesson_learned: Merging an existing archive at runtime requires special handling: make non-permanent symbols permanent, assign classpath indices deterministically based on loader kinds, and free/replace any global filemap state before writing a new archive.

insights.title: Switch to merging only new classes instead of all loaded classes
insights.problem: Previous approach appended all loaded classes into the merged AOT cache which could cause rewriting the cache with unrelated classes and duplicates.
insights.root_cause: No clear separation between previously-archived classes and newly-loaded classes causing the merge to potentially include the whole class set.
insights.solution: Introduce collect_loaded_classes_for_merge to return new_classes and only append those (plus archived ones) to classes_for_merged_aot_cache. Use sets/seen table to avoid duplicates.
insights.lesson_learned: When combining artifacts from an existing archive and runtime-loaded data, explicitly separate archived entries and newly-added entries to avoid unintended duplication or wholesale rewrites.

insights.title: Avoid VM exit handlers that crash destructors during AOT cache creation
insights.problem: Metaspace/AOT cache creation used vm_exit(0) leading to crashes in destructors like ~ThreadTotalCPUTimeClosure().
insights.root_cause: Using vm_exit() in the middle of dump path triggered normal exit path that runs dtor code expecting runtime state that isn't valid in this context.
insights.solution: Replaced vm_exit(0) with vm_direct_exit(0) to bypass normal exit handlers and avoid destructor crashes during AOTCache creation reporting.
insights.lesson_learned: When early-exiting from low-level tooling paths (CDS/AOT), use direct exit forms (vm_direct_exit) to avoid running global destructors that assume a normal runtime state.

insights.title: Lazily init dumptime info when adding verification constraints
insights.problem: add_verification_constraint could crash when DumpTimeClassInfo was null for classes loaded before dump mode.
insights.root_cause: Classes loaded earlier (e.g., via AOT bulk load) had not been registered in dumptime_table because init_dumptime_info ran later.
insights.solution: If the class is non-shared and dumptime_table()->get(k) is null, call init_dumptime_info(k) prior to obtaining info and adding verification constraints.

insights.title: Preserve classfile CRC info across merge runs
insights.problem: During an AOT cache merge run, ClassLoader::record_result() is not invoked and CRC/size info for classes loaded by custom classloaders can be lost, making it impossible to later match unregistered classes by CRC.
insights.root_cause: Merge run differs from a dump run: some recording paths are not executed, so expected dumptime bookkeeping (e.g., ClassLoader::record_result) doesn't populate runtime structures.
insights.solution: Introduce MergeCrcEntry and a _merge_crc_entries array to save classfile size and CRC at class load time (save_classfile_crc_for_merge), and provide apply_saved_merge_crc to copy saved CRC into dumptime info for unregistered classes when preparing merged cache.
insights.lesson_learned: When reusing existing archive metadata in a different runtime mode (merge vs dump), ensure any transient bookkeeping (CRCs, sizes) is explicitly captured and applied because the usual recording hooks might be skipped.

insights.title: Include shared archived classes with null class loader data during merge
insights.problem: Archived classes brought from input archive may have null class_loader_data() during the merge run and were being excluded by loader-alive checks.
insights.root_cause: Merging uses classes present in the input archive; those classes were not loaded during the current run so their CLD may be null but they must still be included into dumptime processing.
insights.solution: Adjust dumptime iteration and validation to include classes that are shared and have null CLD when CDSConfig::is_merging_aot_cache() is true; skip loader-type validation in validate_before_archiving during merge mode.
insights.lesson_learned: Archive-merged classes can have different life-cycle metadata; guard checks must consider merge-mode semantics to avoid accidentally excluding valid archived entries.

insights.title: Add release workflow to build and publish custom JDK images
insights.problem: Manual packaging and release of custom-built JDK images was time-consuming.
insights.root_cause: No CI workflow existed to automate building, packaging, and creating a GitHub release of a built image.
insights.solution: Added a workflow that checks out sources, fetches BootJDK, installs toolchain, configures, builds images, packages them into a tar.gz and creates a GitHub release using gh CLI.

insights.title: Properly handle Class-Path manifest URIs and skip test-classes
insights.problem: Malformed Class-Path entries (e.g., 'file:' URIs from Maven Surefire) produced bogus paths and could lead to incorrect class location handling / recursion.
insights.root_cause: Code concatenated dir_name and file_start without special-casing 'file:' URIs and didn't skip test directories.
insights.solution: Detect 'file:' URIs and convert to filesystem path via uri_to_path; allocate libname accordingly and skip entries containing '/target/test-classes' with a warning.

insights.title: Cache classpath entries to avoid repeatedly opening JARs
insights.problem: is_class_in_current_classpath reopened and statted classpath entries on every call (heavy IO), causing performance issues.
insights.root_cause: Repeated os::stat and ZipLibrary::open per class name lookup was expensive.
insights.solution: Introduce CachedCPEntry array initialized once (init_cached_cp_entries) that stores path, is_dir and an opened jzfile handle for jars; subsequent checks reuse these entries.

insights.title: Skip full app classpath validation when merging caches
insights.problem: During merge flows the app classpath validation could be too strict and unnecessary.
insights.root_cause: Merging uses different semantics and may intentionally skip some classpath checks.
insights.solution: When merging (CDSConfig::is_merging_aot_cache), skip need_to_check_app_classpath branch that performs expensive classpath validation.

insights.title: Add AOTMergeInputs parsing and merge input tracking
insights.problem: Need to support specifying secondary AOT caches to merge via JVM flags.
insights.root_cause: AOT merging previously supported only a single primary input.
insights.solution: Parse AOTMergeInputs into a GrowableArrayCHeap, set CDSConfig::_has_merge_inputs and provide accessors. Validate AOTMergeInputs only usable with AOTMode=merge.

insights.title: Two-phase merge: create preimage config and mark training run
insights.problem: Merging needs a training run (preimage) then a clean assembly; single-phase was fragile.
insights.root_cause: Assembling final archive in same process could copy stale pointers and mix state.
insights.solution: When in merge mode, set a temporary AOTConfiguration (AOTCacheOutput.config) for preimage, enable dumping preimage static archive and mark single-command training to later fork assembly.

insights.title: Add AOTMode=merge and relax AOTCache/AOTCacheOutput assertions
insights.problem: Users need a 'merge' mode that reads an input AOTCache and writes an output AOTCache; previous checks forbade specifying both input and output caches.
insights.root_cause: Original design prevented simultaneous AOTCache and AOTCacheOutput; merge mode requires both an input cache and an output name.
insights.solution: Introduce CDSConfig::is_merging_aot_cache flag, implement check_aotmode_merge that requires AOTCache and enables UseSharedSpaces/RequireSharedSpaces, and relax assertion to allow AOTCache + AOTCacheOutput when mode is 'merge'. Also set AOTCacheOutput default more conservatively in one commit (FLAG_SET_ERGO_IF_DEFAULT).
insights.lesson_learned: When adding a new mode with different flag semantics, update flag validation paths and default-setting logic carefully to avoid surprising exits and to keep backward compatibility for existing users.

insights.title: Expose merge inputs accessors
insights.problem: Other parts of the code need to query merge input paths and count.
insights.root_cause: New AOTMergeInputs array must be accessible via CDSConfig.
insights.solution: Added has_merge_inputs(), num_merge_inputs(), merge_input_at() accessors and storage for _merge_input_paths.

insights.title: Add AOTMergeInputs and AOTDumpArchivedClassList flags
insights.problem: Need flags to specify secondary caches and to request helper VM dumps of archived class lists.
insights.root_cause: Merging design requires auxiliary flags.
insights.solution: Added product flags AOTMergeInputs and AOTDumpArchivedClassList to global CDS flags.

insights.title: AOTCompileEagerly flag demoted from DIAGNOSTIC to EXPERIMENTAL
insights.problem: AOTCompileEagerly was considered diagnostic previously which made it less discoverable/usable by experiments.
insights.root_cause: Incorrect flag classification.
insights.solution: Change product(bool, AOTCompileEagerly, ...) classification from DIAGNOSTIC to EXPERIMENTAL.
insights.lesson_learned: Classify VM flags correctly to reflect intended discoverability and usage; experimental flags must be easy to enable for evaluation.

insights.title: Skip unresolved classes gracefully during create/assembly
insights.problem: When assembling a final image in a merge flow, some classes referenced by recipes may not be resolvable on current classpath and could cause aborts.
insights.root_cause: FinalImageRecipes operated on archive preimage copies assuming resolution/linking would succeed; merge flow can have missing classes.
insights.solution: Maintain _live_klasses array that holds live resolved classes (or nullptr for skipped). Skip recipes whose live class pointer is null; resolve classes at runtime using resolve_or_null and link only live classes, logging and skipping when resolution or linking fails.

insights.title: Nullify final image recipe pointer when writing merge mode
insights.problem: Merging writes preimage and some pointers may be stale for final assembly.
insights.root_cause: FinalImageRecipes serialized pointers can point into old archive memory during merge.
insights.solution: When serializing and writing in merge mode, set _final_image_recipes to nullptr so stale pointers are not serialized.

insights.title: Add _live_klasses to track runtime-resolved classes for recipe application
insights.problem: Need to track which archived classes have live equivalents at assembly time.
insights.root_cause: Preimage copies may not be linkable/usable during final assembly; need mapping to live resolved classes.
insights.solution: Introduce GrowableArray<InstanceKlass*>* _live_klasses and initialize in load_all_classes.

insights.title: Avoid including classes without DumpTimeClassInfo in merge
insights.problem: During merge, pointer-following could encounter classes (e.g., dynamically generated proxies) that were not registered in dumptime_table; attempting to access get_info_locked() crashed.
insights.root_cause: Some classes reachable through CP pointer-following were not part of classes_for_merged_aot_cache and therefore had no dumptime info.
insights.solution: Treat classes with no dumptime_info as excluded in is_excluded() so serialization writes null pointers rather than crashing. Also, for shared classes from input archive not loaded during this run, ensure a DumpTimeClassInfo is allocated if missing.

insights.title: Add AOT map logging at dumptime/runtime
insights.problem: Debugging/inspection of the AOT cache contents required ad-hoc or invasive methods.
insights.root_cause: No centralized mechanism to output detailed map information about archived metaspace and heap objects in both dump-time and runtime usages.
insights.solution: Integrate AOTMapLogger::dumptime_log into ArchiveBuilder::write_archive and wire runtime logging paths; factor out and replace older CDSMapLogger code with a richer AOTMapLogger implementation.
insights.lesson_learned: Adding a dedicated logging facility centralizes map inspection logic and improves debuggability; ensure it is invoked both at dump-time and during runtime initialization where needed.

insights.title: Skip determinism/verification checks when class_loader_data is null
insights.problem: Resolver attempted to verify determinism/loader equality for shared classes whose class_loader_data was null (shared classes from input archive not mapped in this run), causing incorrect assumptions.
insights.root_cause: In merge/assembly flows archive preimage entries may be present without class_loader_data; deterministic checks that rely on class_loader_data would be invalid.
insights.solution: Return false (not deterministic) when cp_holder->class_loader_data() is null; also, when loader data is missing for VM classes, fall back to comparing loader types (defined_by_boot_loader flags) instead of class_loader_data equality.

insights.title: Resolve proxy classes at runtime when dumptime info missing
insights.problem: In merge mode some classes reachable only via constant pool resolution (e.g., java.lang.reflect.Proxy) had no DumpTimeClassInfo and were being treated as excluded/unresolvable.
insights.root_cause: Dumptime table entries exist only for classes added to classes_for_merged_aot_cache; pointer-followed classes may lack entries.
insights.solution: When in merge mode, if dumptime_table()->get(ik) is null for a non-shared class, treat resolution as non-deterministic (return false) or allow runtime resolution; also check SystemDictionaryShared::is_excluded_class only after dumptime checks.

insights.title: Handle hash collisions in code entry lookup by verifying stored name
insights.problem: Binary search and id-based lookup could return an entry with same kind+id but for a different name due to id collisions.
insights.root_cause: IDs are derived from hashed values; different names may collide to same id. Previous code assumed id and kind were unique.
insights.solution: Enhance check_entry to, when name and cache buffer provided, verify stored_name matches provided name (using name_offset/name_size). Pass the name into find_entry and use buffer pointer when available. Linear search fallback still used to scan neighborhood.

insights.title: Free _stubs_addr in AOTCodeAddressTable destructor
insights.problem: _stubs_addr pointer was not initialized and not freed leading to potential leaks or double frees/uninitialized access.
insights.root_cause: Constructor didn't initialize _stubs_addr to nullptr and destructor didn't check/free it.
insights.solution: Initialize _stubs_addr to nullptr in header and added destructor check to FREE_C_HEAP_ARRAY for _stubs_addr when not null.
insights.lesson_learned: Always initialize pointer members in constructors and ensure destructors free resources only when non-null to avoid leaks and UB.

insights.title: Fix ASAN-reported heap-buffer-overflow in copy_bytes
insights.problem: Custom word/byte copy logic used Copy::disjoint_words/Copy::conjoint_jbytes and calculated word counts with an expression that could overrun buffer bounds under some size inputs leading to heap-buffer-overflow under ASAN.
insights.root_cause: Complex custom copy logic and word-size rounding introduced off-by-one or oversized copying due to ((size + HeapWordSize - 1) / HeapWordSize) with mismatched pointer types and signedness.
insights.solution: Replace custom copy logic with a safe memcpy(to, from, size) and simplify the logging message. Use assert casting to int for size checks to avoid signedness pitfalls.
insights.lesson_learned: Low-level memory copy code is error-prone; prefer standard library primitives (memcpy) unless wordwise copies are necessary for performance, and if implemented carefully validate signedness/rounding. ASAN is valuable in catching such bugs.

insights.title: Enable AOT code caching only on supported platforms
insights.problem: AOT code caching attempted to initialize on unsupported platforms (e.g., Zero/unsupported architectures) causing incorrect behavior.
insights.root_cause: No platform guard in initialize() allowed unsupported combinations to reach AOT initialization code.
insights.solution: Add preprocessor guard to early-return and disable AOTAdapterCaching when not AMD64 or AARCH64 (or running Zero).
insights.lesson_learned: Guard platform-specific features with compile-time checks; tests should also reflect required platforms.

insights.title: Expose optional name parameter for find_entry
insights.problem: Need to pass the looked-up name into find_entry to disambiguate collisions.
insights.root_cause: Find-entry previously only accepted kind and encoded id.
insights.solution: Change signature to find_entry(kind, id, const char* name = nullptr).

insights.title: Initialize _stubs_addr to nullptr in AOTCodeAddressTable
insights.problem: _stubs_addr left uninitialized could lead to freeing garbage pointer.
insights.root_cause: Missing initializer in constructor.
insights.solution: Set _stubs_addr(nullptr) in constructor initializer list.
insights.lesson_learned: Initialize all members including auxiliary address arrays to avoid UB during destruction.

insights.title: Avoid loading cached classes whose class files are missing on current classpath
insights.problem: Loading an archived class when its source JAR/classpath isn't available could lead to mismatched dependencies at runtime.
insights.root_cause: SystemDictionary::is_shared_class_visible previously checked module/location but didn't verify presence on current app classpath in merge scenarios.
insights.solution: For app-defined classes (defined_by_app_loader, not hidden), if archived classpath index indicates not visible, check for existence of the .class file on current classpath via AOTClassLocationConfig::is_class_in_current_classpath and return false if not found.

insights.title: Change start_merging_aot_cache signature to accept TRAPS and add symbol allocation query
insights.problem: New merge flow needs to call start_merging_aot_cache from contexts with TRAPS and needs to query symbol allocatability.
insights.root_cause: start_merging_aot_cache previously had no TRAPS param; symbol allocation decisions required exposing symbol_space_is_allocatable.
insights.solution: Modify declaration to start_merging_aot_cache(TRAPS) and add symbol_space_is_allocatable() accessor.

insights.title: Guard symbol allocation when dumping static archive
insights.problem: Symbol allocation for deterministic dump used the dump region unconditionally; when symbol region isn't allocatable, it could cause issues.
insights.root_cause: CDS dump path attempted to allocate symbol nodes even when symbol region wasn't available.
insights.solution: Only use DumpRegion_lock allocation when dumping static archive AND MetaspaceShared::symbol_space_is_allocatable() is true.

insights.title: Nullify archived arrays when serializing in merge mode
insights.problem: In merge mode arrays contained stale pointers from the old archive which must not be serialized into the preimage.
insights.root_cause: Merging writes a preimage that should not include pointers referencing an already-mounted archive.
insights.solution: In serialize(), when writing and in merging mode, set _boot/_boot2/_platform/_app to nullptr before serialization.

insights.title: Reset runtime heap tables when writing preimage during merge
insights.problem: Tables in heapShared contained stale pointers when merging and would serialize invalid addresses.
insights.root_cause: Merging doesn't dump heap; yet writing preimage could walk tables referencing the old archive.
insights.solution: When soc->writing() and CDSConfig::is_merging_aot_cache(), reset specific archived pointers/tables (_archived_ArchiveHeapTestClass, _run_time_subgraph_info_table, _run_time_special_subgraph) before serialization.

insights.title: Allow dumping while using an archive for merge mode
insights.problem: An assertion prevented dumping a static archive while an archive was in use, but merge mode needs to run with the input archive mapped.
insights.root_cause: Previous invariant assumed dumps only occur when not using an archive; merge-at-runtime breaks that assumption.
insights.solution: Remove the strict guarantee and allow dump to proceed when using an archive in merge mode.
insights.lesson_learned: Global invariants about 'not using archive during dump' must be re-evaluated when introducing merge-at-runtime capabilities.

insights.title: Nullify static invokers pointer when writing preimage
insights.problem: Static archive invokers table could contain stale data when preimage is written.
insights.root_cause: Merging should not serialize stale archived invokers.
insights.solution: When writing in merge mode set _static_archive_invokers to nullptr before serialization.

insights.title: Reset archived loader data when serializing in merge mode
insights.problem: Archived loader data could point into an input archive causing invalid serialized state.
insights.root_cause: Preimage should not carry references to previously-built archives' loader structures.
insights.solution: When writing and merging, zero-out archived loader data fields prior to serialization.

insights.title: Save classfile CRC for merge when creating classes not in dump mode
insights.problem: During merge, need to record classfile CRCs for classes that were loaded during training run so they can be matched at assembly by CRC lookup.
insights.root_cause: ClassLoader::record_result only runs in archive dumping mode; merge training run needs CRC recording when not fully dumping.
insights.solution: When merging and not dumping archive, for non-hidden classes record classfile CRCs via SystemDictionaryShared::save_classfile_crc_for_merge(result, stream).

insights.title: Reset shared string table when writing preimage in merge mode
insights.problem: Shared string table could contain invalid references during preimage serialization.
insights.root_cause: Merging writes a preimage and should not serialize tables referencing old archives.
insights.solution: When writing and merging, reset _shared_table before serializing header.

insights.title: CDS dump: prevent addition of interned strings and ensure safe snapshot
insights.problem: AOT (CDS) shared string table creation failed due to strings being added while dumping, or wrong item counts used causing 'no strings should have been added' or incorrect sizing leading to failures.
insights.root_cause: CDS dumping assumed only a single Java thread and that no compilation tasks were active; but background compiler tasks could still be active and intern() could race during dumping. Also the code used non-atomic reads of _items_count leading to untrusted values during dump.
insights.solution: Introduced CompileBroker::wait_for_no_active_tasks() to wait for JIT tasks to finish before proceeding, added atomic acquire loads for _items_count via items_count_acquire(), added a DEBUG flag to assert no intern() calls during dump and assert preconditions (single Java thread), and guarded freeing/writing with explicit acquire/release semantics. Also fixed initialization of VerifyCompStrings to use items_count_acquire().
insights.lesson_learned: When taking global snapshots that depend on stable counts, ensure background subsystems (compilation threads) are quiesced and use atomic operations to read shared counters; add assertions to detect invalid concurrent operations during critical phases like CDS dumps.

insights.title: Handle resolved references for shared classes not loaded during assembly
insights.problem: remove_unshareable_info asserted conditions assuming unregistered classes were not loaded, but in merge flows shared classes may be present with no class_loader_data and resolved_reference_length already saved in input archive.
insights.root_cause: ConstantPool handling assumed normal record→create flow; in merge, preimage may refer to shared classes whose info was pre-populated in input archive.
insights.solution: Adjust condition to treat CDSConfig::is_merging_aot_cache() same as is_dumping_final_static_archive() for the resolved_reference_length preconditions, and handle src_holder->is_shared() && src_holder->class_loader_data() == nullptr specially.

insights.title: Reset AOT adapter handler table when serializing in merge mode
insights.problem: AOT adapter handler table pointed into old archives when writing preimage.
insights.root_cause: Preimage serialization should avoid embedding stale pointers.
insights.solution: When writing and merging, clear _aot_adapter_handler_table prior to serialize_shared_table_header.

insights.title: Expose merge CRC helper APIs
insights.problem: Needed to store and apply CRC/size information for merge mode but header lacked declarations.
insights.root_cause: New merge functionality requires new helper functions to be accessible from other compilation units.
insights.solution: Add declarations for save_classfile_crc_for_merge and apply_saved_merge_crc.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding a new cross-cutting behavior (merge-time CRC handling), expose small focused helpers in the header to keep implementation modular.

insights.title: Treat archived classes with null classloader data as alive in merge mode
insights.problem: Classes coming from the input archive can have null class_loader_data() during a merge run and were previously skipped by 'loader alive' checks.
insights.root_cause: Merge mode operates against an existing archive; some class metadata (CLD) is validly null because they were archived rather than loaded during this run.
insights.solution: Modify iteration to include k->is_shared() && k->class_loader_data() == nullptr cases and invoke function(k, info) for them when CDSConfig::is_merging_aot_cache() is true.
insights.lesson_learned: Iteration logic that assumes in-memory loader metadata exists must be adapted when operating in modes that reuse persisted archive metadata.

insights.title: Relax assertions for shared classes in merge mode
insights.problem: Debug assertions prevented creating/getting dumptime info for shared classes unless doing a final static archive dump, but merge mode legitimately touches shared classes.
insights.root_cause: Assertions assumed only final static archive operations would handle shared classes; merge mode also needs those codepaths.
insights.solution: Extend assertions to allow CDSConfig::is_merging_aot_cache() as an allowed context.
insights.lesson_learned: Debug guards must be updated alongside new feature modes; otherwise they can cause spurious assertion failures during legit uses.

insights.title: Introduce AOTMapLogger to print AOT cache contents
insights.problem: Need human-readable mapfile output for AOT caches (static or runtime) to help diagnose content/layout issues.
insights.root_cause: No existing facility that prints detailed metaspace/heap object mapping consistently between dump-time and runtime.
insights.solution: Add AOTMapLogger class with dumptime_log and runtime_log APIs, plus utilities for translating buffer/requested addresses and printing typed metadata details.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding diagnostic tooling, provide both dump-time and runtime entrypoints and ensure address translations for consistent reporting.

insights.title: Add helpers to interpret buffered heap oop metadata for map logging
insights.problem: Map logging needed to interpret objects stored in the archive buffers (determine klass and size) but existing helpers didn't expose convenient APIs.
insights.root_cause: Archive buffered memory layout needs readable helpers to produce map outputs and to inspect archived heap objects.
insights.solution: Add real_klass_of_buffered_oop and size_of_buffered_oop helpers, and keep the buffered->requested address translation functions.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding map/inspection features, expose small translation helpers to simplify higher-level logging code and to avoid re-implementing address arithmetic across modules.

insights.title: Expose buffered oop utilities to header
insights.problem: New functions used by logging code needed declarations.
insights.root_cause: Header didn't declare new helper functions used by AOTMapLogger and other code.
insights.solution: Declare real_klass_of_buffered_oop and size_of_buffered_oop in header.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep implementation and header synchronized when adding helpers used across translation units.

insights.title: Avoid retaining many CompileTask objects in free list after spikes
insights.problem: Compilation spikes left many CompileTask objects in a free-list; the freelist recycling semantics were complex and could leave large numbers of objects retained.
insights.root_cause: Old design used a freelist under a global allocation lock and relied on conventions about which thread frees a task; this made it easy to accumulate many tasks and complicated life-cycle reasoning.
insights.solution: Remove freelist-based recycling: create tasks with new, delete them when done, rename free_all to delete_all, and adapt callers to delete tasks rather than recycle. Adjust comments and behavior accordingly.
insights.lesson_learned: Simpler ownership (allocate-with-new, delete-when-done) reduces subtle lifetime bugs and avoids global freelist complexity under spikes; use atomic counters for active tasks and well-defined wait/notify semantics.

insights.title: Wait for active compile tasks before CDS string table dump
insights.problem: CDS creation could proceed while JIT compilation tasks still active, causing intern table mutations during dump.
insights.root_cause: No mechanism existed to wait for active CompileTask instances to finish before starting CDS dump.
insights.solution: Added CompileBroker::wait_for_no_active_tasks() which delegates to CompileTask::wait_for_no_active_tasks() to block until compiler tasks have drained.
insights.lesson_learned: When global operations depend on quiescent background work, provide explicit join/wait APIs in the broker/manager objects responsible for those tasks.

insights.title: Remove freelist for CompileTask; use ctor/dtor and active_tasks counter
insights.problem: Freelist management added complexity and potential to retain many objects during load spikes. Waiting/wakeup semantics were tied to freelist state.
insights.root_cause: Manual freelist plus Monitor-based allocator led to brittle logic under concurrency and peaks.
insights.solution: Remove static freelist and is_free flags. Add explicit constructor/destructor to manage JNI handles and failure_reason; increment/decrement atomic _active_tasks and notify waiters when count drops to zero. Replace allocate/free with new/delete usage.
insights.lesson_learned: Switching to RAII-like patterns and atomic counters simplifies lifetime and waiting logic and makes behavior under spikes predictable.

insights.title: Track active compile tasks and provide wait/notify semantics
insights.problem: There was no robust way to wait for all active CompileTask instances to finish; potential races when allocation/free occurred.
insights.root_cause: CompileTask allocation/free did not update a shared active counter and used MutexLocker which didn't support notify/wait semantics; free didn't notify waiting threads when last task freed.
insights.solution: Added static _active_tasks counter incremented on allocate and decremented on free, changed locking from MutexLocker to MonitorLocker for CompileTaskAlloc_lock to support wait/notify, and implemented CompileTask::wait_for_no_active_tasks() which waits on the monitor until _active_tasks is zero.
insights.lesson_learned: If a component must allow other threads to wait on state changes, use synchronization primitives that support wait/notify and maintain explicit counters; avoid hiding semantics behind mutex types that lack needed features.

insights.title: Rename free_all to delete_all in compile queue API
insights.problem: Method name free_all implied freelist recycling which was removed.
insights.root_cause: API needed to reflect new semantics (deleting tasks instead of reusing freelist nodes).
insights.solution: Rename method to delete_all and update callers.
insights.lesson_learned: API names should reflect ownership semantics; renames help avoid confusion when behavior changes.

insights.title: CompileBroker exposes wait_for_no_active_tasks API
insights.problem: No public contract to wait for active compile tasks.
insights.root_cause: Higher-level code (CDS) needs to ensure compilation quiescence but could not do so via existing API.
insights.solution: Added static declaration of wait_for_no_active_tasks() to the CompileBroker interface.
insights.lesson_learned: Broker/manager headers should expose synchronization primitives needed by consumers that perform global operations.

insights.title: Remove CompileTaskAlloc_lock monitor
insights.problem: Global monitor used only for freelist allocation was removed; leftover declaration needed cleanup.
insights.root_cause: Freelist-based allocation gone, so its lock was unnecessary.
insights.solution: Remove MUTEX_DEFL for CompileTaskAlloc_lock and its extern declaration.
insights.lesson_learned: Eliminate locks and monitors tied to removed data structures to avoid unused global state and confusion.

insights.title: Use Monitor for CompileTaskAlloc_lock to allow wait/notify
insights.problem: CompileTaskAlloc_lock was a Mutex, but code needed monitor semantics (wait/notify) to coordinate active compile tasks.
insights.root_cause: Incorrect lock type (Mutex) was used for an allocation lock that needs monitor behavior.
insights.solution: Changed declaration and initialization of CompileTaskAlloc_lock from Mutex* to Monitor* and updated macro usage to PaddedMonitor so MonitorLocker can be used.
insights.lesson_learned: Choose synchronization primitives that match required semantics (monitor vs mutex). When changing, update both declaration and initialization sites.

insights.title: Remove external declaration for CompileTaskAlloc_lock
insights.problem: Header declared a Mutex* for freelist allocation which is no longer used.
insights.root_cause: Freelist removed from CompileTask implementation.
insights.solution: Remove extern Mutex* CompileTaskAlloc_lock declaration.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep header declarations aligned with implementation to avoid stale symbols.

insights.title: Change CompileTaskAlloc_lock type to Monitor in header
insights.problem: Header declared CompileTaskAlloc_lock as Mutex* while implementation needs Monitor*.
insights.root_cause: Mismatch between header and implementation for lock type.
insights.solution: Updated extern declaration to Monitor*.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep lock type declarations consistent between header and implementation; mismatches can lead to subtle build/runtime issues.

insights.title: Enhance CDS map test to create and execute AOT map logging
insights.problem: Existing test only exercised static dump logging; need to validate runtime logging as well.
insights.root_cause: AOT map logging feature added; tests must exercise both dumptime and runtime codepaths.
insights.solution: Modify test to create an archive with aot+map logging and then execute a JVM using the archive with runtime aot+map logging, validate outputs.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding both dumptime and runtime diagnostic features, update tests to validate both modes; ensure logfile size flags (filesize=0) to capture entire output.

insights.title: New AOTMapTest to validate aot+map logging in AOT workflow
insights.problem: Need an automated test that covers aot+map logging across AOT workflows (assembly/dump/run).
insights.root_cause: AOT map logger feature introduced; requires coverage for both static/dynamic assembly and runtime use.
insights.solution: Add AOTMapTest to build a small app, run assembly/dump dynamic and runtime runs with -Xlog:aot+map logging and validate the produced map files using CDSMapReader.
insights.lesson_learned: Comprehensive diagnostic features require tests that exercise all relevant AOT workflows and both dump-time and runtime logging.

insights.title: Active Settings view broken / JFR view column FORMAT line wrapping
