insights.problem: A continued FORMAT line was broken across lines causing view configuration parsing/formatting to be incorrect and the Active Settings view to be broken.
insights.root_cause: Line splitting in the configuration left mismatched FORMAT tokens/commas across lines which the view parser expects to be a single continuous entry.
insights.solution: Reflowed/merged the FORMAT entries to be on a single consistent line so the configuration parser sees the expected format tokens.
insights.lesson_learned: Be careful when editing .ini/table-format lines to keep logical entries intact; view parsing expects exact format fields. Small whitespace/line breaks in config files can break UI views.

insights.title: Clarified labels and SQL ordering for JFR method views
insights.problem: Labels and SELECT clauses for method sample views were inconsistent and lacked ordering, causing confusing UI and unpredictable ordering.
insights.root_cause: View config used imprecise labels and SELECT statements without ORDER BY and normalized format settings.
insights.solution: Adjusted labels for clarity and changed SELECT clause to include COUNT alias and ORDER BY C DESC, simplified FORMAT tokens.
insights.lesson_learned: View definitions should include explicit ordering and clear labels to avoid surprises in UI displays.

insights.title: Fix column order and labels in Method Timing view
insights.problem: Method timing view displayed columns in a confusing order and used inconsistent labels (Min. Time vs Minimum Time).
insights.root_cause: Query SELECT ordering didn't match the intended display order and labels were inconsistent.
insights.solution: Reordered SELECT to show Minimum, Average, Maximum and updated labels to 'Minimum Time' etc.
insights.lesson_learned: Ensure UI/view definitions match event field semantics and order to avoid confusing users.

insights.title: Missing acquire semantics when reading _extra_data_lock
insights.problem: Reader side loaded pointer to _extra_data_lock without acquire ordering, risking seeing stale data or reordering leading to race conditions.
insights.root_cause: Atomic::load was used instead of Atomic::load_acquire when reading a lock pointer that may have been installed concurrently.
insights.solution: Replace Atomic::load with Atomic::load_acquire to ensure proper acquire semantics on the reader side.
insights.lesson_learned: When publishing synchronization primitives (locks) you must use appropriate atomic memory-ordering (release on writer, acquire on reader). Prefer explicit acquire loads when reading pointers installed concurrently.

insights.title: invokeinterface exception semantics and overpass handling
insights.problem: invokeinterface resolution could check loader constraints for JVM-created overpass methods and incorrectly decide exception types; also conditional logic produced confusing error handling paths.
insights.root_cause: Overpass methods (created by JVM to throw exceptions) were not excluded from loader-constraint checks; some conditional branches and assert logic were convoluted and could result in wrong exception types being thrown.
insights.solution: Added guard to skip loader-constraint checks for overpass methods, simplified checks in initialize_itable_for_interface to not treat overpass specially where not needed, and reworked some conditions/ordering to ensure IllegalAccessError or AbstractMethodError are inserted correctly.
insights.lesson_learned: Special JVM-generated constructs (like overpass methods) must be explicitly excluded from normal resolution/constraint checks. Keep conditional logic clear to avoid surprising exception type changes.

insights.title: Strengthened test expectations to exact exception types
insights.problem: Tests used throws_ which allowed subclass or broader exceptions, making assertions ambiguous regarding exact exception type produced (AbstractMethodError vs ICCE).
insights.root_cause: Test API allowed looser exception matching. The underlying VM change made exact exception type semantics important to assert.
insights.solution: Changed tests to use throwsExact(...) to assert precise exception types for multiple call-site scenarios and added additional call-site cases to exercise invokeinterface behaviour.
insights.lesson_learned: When VM behaviour differentiates between exception types, tests must assert exact exceptions to detect regressions. Prefer throwsExact in tests that verify precise JVM semantics.

insights.title: Problem-listing a test for a specific platform
insights.problem: serviceability/sa/ClhsdbThreadContext.java failing on Windows due to earlier change (JDK-8356704).
insights.root_cause: Regressions introduced by previous change made test unstable/unsupported on specific platform; rather than fixing test immediately, it is problem-listed for windows-x64.
insights.solution: Added entry mapping test to bug id and platform to skip in CI.
insights.lesson_learned: ProblemList.txt is used to opt-out problematic tests on particular platforms pending proper fixes; include the bug tracking id and platform.

insights.title: Remove workaround for StartupOutput.java
insights.problem: StartupOutput.java was listed as a windows-all problem after prior failures.
insights.root_cause: Workaround entry remained after test itself was fixed.
insights.solution: Removed the problem-list entry for compiler/startup/StartupOutput.java.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep ProblemList in sync when tests are fixed to avoid hiding issues or falsely skipping platforms.

insights.title: Test server lacks support for SERVER307; skip sequence
insights.problem: Test server didn't support certain redirect/auth combinations (SERVER307) which caused failures.
insights.root_cause: Test harness or server implementation incomplete for PROXY305/SERVER307 cases.
insights.solution: Skip SERVER307 in the test loops alongside PROXY305.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding protocol/behavior checks, ensure the test server supports all tested cases or explicitly skip unsupported ones to avoid noise in CI.

insights.title: TLS handshake message ordering validation for Certificate
insights.problem: Certificate messages could be processed without verifying preceding EncryptedExtensions, allowing unexpected handshake ordering.
insights.root_cause: Handshake consumer map was used to detect presence of consumers but logic confused presence-check order; missing check for ENCRYPTED_EXTENSIONS presence before Certificate in TLS 1.3 flow.
insights.solution: Added explicit check to ensure ENCRYPTED_EXTENSIONS had been processed (if present) before accepting Certificate; throw UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE on violation.
insights.lesson_learned: TLS handshake processing must validate message ordering strictly; add explicit checks and fail-fast when order violates protocol assumptions.

insights.title: ReverseBytes constant-folding must respect Java subword casts
insights.problem: reverse_bytes used checked_cast<jshort/jchar> on int constant which could produce mismatched values and cause asserts during C2 compilation.
insights.root_cause: Using checked_cast while constant was held as int could mismatch Java semantics where an int passed to a method expecting short/char is truncated to that smaller type before operation.
insights.solution: Use static_cast<jshort/jchar> on the int constant before byteswap so behavior matches Java truncation semantics (and keep int/int64 cases unchanged).
insights.lesson_learned: JVM compiler IR constant-folding must model Java value truncation semantics (subword types) correctly, especially for methods accepting smaller types. Use correct cast not checked_cast which may assert.

insights.title: Constant folding for ReverseBytes nodes
insights.problem: ReverseBytes nodes were not constant-folded in C2 GVN, preventing compile-time simplification when operand is a singleton constant.
insights.root_cause: ReverseBytesNode lacked a Value() implementation delegating to a byteswap of singleton constants.
insights.solution: Added reverse_bytes helper and implemented ReverseBytesNode::Value() to return folded TypeInt/TypeLong for singleton constants.
insights.lesson_learned: Ensure ops that are pure bit-manipulations implement constant folding handling for singleton types in Value(), improving generated code and eliminating runtime nodes.

insights.title: Added helper jasm to exercise ReverseBytes for short/char paths
insights.problem: Need direct bytecode-level helpers to force inlining/compile-time folding of reverseBytes on subword types.
insights.root_cause: Existing java helpers didn't exercise the exact method signatures; JASM helper gives precise signatures to test compiler.
insights.solution: Added ReverseBytesConstantsHelper.jasm with methods reverseBytesShort and reverseBytesChar accepting int and calling Short.reverseBytes/Character.reverseBytes with smaller descriptor.
insights.lesson_learned: Low-level JASM helpers are useful to create exact callsite signatures to reproduce compiler corner-cases.

insights.title: Extend ReverseBytes constant-folding tests and prevent REVERSE_BYTES IR nodes
insights.problem: Existing tests did not cover cases where int-to-short/char truncation should be applied and C2 produced IR nodes or calls unexpectedly.
insights.root_cause: Test didn't inline helper and didn't include tests for additional constant scenarios.
insights.solution: Added compile-time inline flag, more tests for subword cases, and new IR-based checks to assert absence of ReverseBytes and CALL nodes where constant-folding should happen.
insights.lesson_learned: Add explicit IR-level assertions in compiler tests and ensure helper classes are inlined to catch optimization/regression scenarios.

insights.title: GVN tests to ensure ReverseBytes constant-folding
insights.problem: Need to validate that ReverseBytes operations get folded out of IR by C2 GVN.
insights.root_cause: New folding logic requires regression tests to ensure it remains effective.
insights.solution: Add tests covering int/long/short/char reverseBytes cases and assert IR node absence.
insights.lesson_learned: Compiler IR changes must be backed by unit/IR-level tests that assert absence of nodes (failOn).

insights.title: Pointer arithmetic in card table assertions was using wrong base
insights.problem: ASSERT computed end_bp as &(new_ptr)[_card_table->last_valid_index()] but new_ptr did not represent the start of the write_byte_map leading to incorrect pointer range checks in ASSERT.
insights.root_cause: Used new_ptr variable instead of start_bp base pointer when computing end pointer for assertion range check.
insights.solution: Compute end_bp relative to start_bp: &(start_bp[_card_table->last_valid_index()]) to match the buffer area being checked.
insights.lesson_learned: ASSERTs that compute pointer ranges should use the same base used by the buffer to avoid false positives; careful with pointer arithmetic and variable naming.

insights.title: SuperWord truncation: subword operations incorrectly truncated inputs
insights.problem: SuperWord/vectorization assumed some ops could truncate inputs (treat int inputs as smaller types) causing wrong results for CLZ/CTZ/reverse/bitCount for byte/short inputs.
insights.root_cause: Vectorization allowed truncation for operations that are NOT truncation-safe (like CountLeadingZeros, Reverse, PopCount) for subword types; code relied on container_type/load size incorrectly.
insights.solution: Introduced can_subword_truncate() to explicitly enumerate truncation-safe opcodes and disallow truncation for others; changed compute_vector_element_type() to use node type (container_type) when widening and to consult can_subword_truncate. Tightened assertions and fallback logic.
insights.lesson_learned: Vectorization must be conservative about truncation semantics: operations whose result depends on higher-order bits cannot be safely truncated. Encapsulate truncation safety checks in a helper function and enumerate safe/unsafe ops.

insights.title: pusha_uncached must restore RAX contents correctly
insights.problem: pusha_uncached pushed pairs and did stack ops but didn't restore original RAX contents leading to incorrect register restoration when APX or special flows used.
insights.root_cause: Missing movq(rax, Address(rax)) to restore original RAX before further pushes/stack ops in a 64-bit context.
insights.solution: Inserted movq(rax, Address(rax)) to restore original contents of RAX register in pusha_uncached.
insights.lesson_learned: Low-level register save/restore sequences must ensure any temporary uses of registers are reversed before pushing others; small omissions can corrupt register state.

insights.title: APX extended registers must be saved/restored in Shenandoah barrier stubs
insights.problem: When Intel APX (extended GP regs r16–r31) is enabled, Shenandoah barrier stubs didn't allocate or save/restore APX registers, causing test failures/crashes when APX enabled.
insights.root_cause: Number of saved registers didn't account for APX registers and code didn't conditionally save/restore them based on UseAPX flag.
insights.solution: Adjusted num_saved_regs to include APX regs when UseAPX is true and added movptr saves and restores for r16..r31 guarded by UseAPX checks.
insights.lesson_learned: Target-specific features (APX) affect calling/save conventions; assembler code must be conditionalized to save/restore extended registers when the feature is enabled.

insights.title: Disable APX by default and require explicit VM flags to enable
insights.problem: APX support was implicitly enabled by default in non-PRODUCT builds; this caused instability and regressions.
insights.root_cause: Earlier logic auto-enabled APX based on CPUID and OS support in some builds; this led to inconsistent behavior across product vs debug builds and unexpected crashes.
insights.solution: Remove default auto-enablement of UseAPX; require -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:+UseAPX to enable APX. Remove some #ifndef PRODUCT gating so APX disabled by default.
insights.lesson_learned: New CPU features should be opt-in until fully validated across builds/platforms. Don't rely on build-type conditionals that create different default behaviors silently.

insights.title: Correct AVX3Threshold platform predicate
insights.problem: AVX3Threshold defaulting logic used is_intel_family_core() which was incorrect for some platforms resulting in wrong threshold and buffer overflows.
insights.root_cause: Predicate used the wrong family test; should use server family detection.
insights.solution: Changed test from is_intel_family_core() to is_intel_server_family() when deciding to set avx3_threshold to 0 when AVX3Threshold flag is default.
insights.lesson_learned: Feature/threshold defaults need accurate platform classification; incorrect predicates can lead to unsafe defaults.

insights.title: Populate feature bitmap and CPUID AVX10 parsing
insights.problem: Need to populate the extended feature bitmap from CPUID leaves and handle AVX10 converged ISA fields.
insights.root_cause: Addition of VM_Features requires new parsing and population code.
insights.solution: Updated CPUID parsing code (omitted diff) to fill VM_Features/_cpu_features and provide helper to insert feature names.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing feature representation, update CPUID parsing and any native/string output code consistently.

insights.title: APX-related exception handling removed for product builds
insights.problem: Conditional preprocessor logic that previously only ran in non-PRODUCT builds was simplified to always require explicit APX handling; some APX related SEGV handling code removed.
insights.root_cause: Part of change to make APX disabled by default and require explicit enabling; removed #if !defined(PRODUCT) guards and related code.
insights.solution: Removed the conditional blocks so APX detection/handling is not implicitly done in non-PRODUCT builds; behavior changes require explicit EnableAPX.
insights.lesson_learned: Changing default CPU-feature flags impacts OS-specific signal handling code; ensure platform-specific handlers align with new defaults.

insights.title: Documented IndexOutOfBoundsException on parameterSlot
insights.problem: CodeBuilder::parameterSlot could throw an undocumented IndexOutOfBoundsException which client code/tests rely on.
insights.root_cause: API javadoc didn't document the exception thrown for out-of-range parameter index.
insights.solution: Added @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException javadoc to parameterSlot contract.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep API Javadoc in sync with runtime exceptions to help callers and tests rely on stable documented behavior.

insights.title: Test for parameterSlot IOOBE and receiver slot behavior
insights.problem: Tests didn't assert IndexOutOfBoundsException for invalid indices and didn't check receiverSlot IllegalState for static methods.
insights.root_cause: Missing negative tests for edge indices and receiver slot on static methods.
insights.solution: Added assertions for negative and out-of-range indexes and receiverSlot IllegalStateException when appropriate.
insights.lesson_learned: When API throws checked/unchecked exceptions for bad input, tests should assert exact exception behavior including extreme indices.

insights.title: CodeBlob::purge and constructor assert misuse and mutable sizes initialization
insights.problem: Assertions used assignment (assert(_mutable_data = blob_end())) and relocation_size derived from pointer arithmetic could be invalid when _mutable_data is null leading to UBSAN or crashes; mutable sizes not initialized leading to applying offsets to null.
insights.root_cause: Using assignment instead of equality in assert, not initializing _mutable_data_size/_relocation_size in some code paths, and computing relocation_size via pointer arithmetic relying on relocation_end() which could be null.
insights.solution: Fixed asserts to use equality checks, initialized _mutable_data_size to 0 in constructor, set mutable defaults in restore_mutable_data (set _mutable_data = blob_end() when no reloc_data), and changed relocation_size() accessor to return stored _relocation_size instead of computing via pointer arithmetic.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid assert expressions that perform assignments; initialize size fields consistently and avoid pointer-delta computations on possibly-null pointers—store sizes explicitly.

insights.title: nmethod::purge must clear JVMCI metadata size
insights.problem: JVMCI code accessed nmethod metadata (jvmci_name) after nmethod purge where _metadata_size wasn't reset leading to crashes.
insights.root_cause: nmethod::purge didn't clear _metadata_size before CodeBlob::purge which cleared mutable data and could leave metadata_size inconsistent.
insights.solution: Set _metadata_size = 0 in JVMCI-only block before calling CodeBlob::purge.
insights.lesson_learned: When clearing or purging objects with layered state, ensure all derived/related metadata fields are reset in the correct order to prevent stale references.

insights.title: Backed out changes related to relocation updates and locking in nmethod
insights.problem: A prior change introducing extra locking and relocation updates caused regressions; this commit backs out those changes.
insights.root_cause: The previous change attempted to use ConditionalMutexLocker and relocation updates that led to a complex/fragile interaction (race/deadlock or incorrect relocation handling).
insights.solution: Removed the previously added conditional critical section and relocation info update code to restore prior behavior.
insights.lesson_learned: Backouts indicate approaches that seemed plausible introduced instability—when manipulating relocation info or locking around patching, ensure strong invariants and tests for races; be conservative when changing locking order.

insights.title: GuardedMemory support for a second tag and more robust printing
insights.problem: JNI checked wrappers needed to distinguish allocations from different sources (GetStringChars/GetPrimitiveArrayCritical) but GuardedMemory had only one tag field; print_on also lacked tag2.
insights.root_cause: GuardedMemory API had single tag; jniCheck needed to annotate allocations with second tag to validate release calls correctly.
insights.solution: Extended wrap_copy and GuardedMemory to carry tag2, added tag2 getters/setters, updated print_on formatting to include tag2 and added os.hpp include. Updated wrap_copy callsites accordingly and tests.
insights.lesson_learned: Adding small auxiliary metadata (tag2) can enable better diagnostics and validated runtime checks. Keep print/diagnostic helpers updated when adding metadata.

insights.title: GuardHeader extended with tag2 and verify uses os::is_readable_range
insights.problem: GuardHeader verify could attempt to dereference unmapped memory leading to crashes; header lacked second tag.
insights.root_cause: verify assumed guard pointers are readable; when testing unmapped regions this can UB/crash.
insights.solution: Added os::is_readable_range check in verify to return false safely for unmapped ranges; added _tag2 field and accessors; expanded docs/comments to include tag2 layout.
insights.lesson_learned: Diagnostic wrappers that may operate on possibly-unmapped memory must avoid dereferencing memory directly; add OS-level checks to guard verification routines.

insights.title: Checked JNI release functions must filter out wrapped arrays from different allocators
insights.problem: Checked Release<type>ArrayElements didn't detect arrays that were actually wrappers from other JNI functions (GetStringChars/GetStringUTFChars/GetPrimitiveArrayCritical), leading to misleading/missing error reporting or incorrect behavior.
insights.root_cause: JNI wrappers used same wrapping scheme but had no secondary tag to indicate origin, and existing check_wrapped_array didn't validate source or tag differences.
insights.solution: Introduce well-known tag constants (STRING_TAG, STRING_UTF_TAG, CRITICAL_TAG), pass is_critical into wrapping, extend check_wrapped_array to accept is_critical and check guarded.get_tag2() to ensure caller matches allocation origin, and emit fatal errors for mismatches. Adjust check_jni_wrap_copy_array to pass CRITICAL_TAG when appropriate.
insights.lesson_learned: Runtime checked wrappers must carry origin metadata and validation must check origin when matching release calls. Use distinct markers for different allocator sources.

insights.title: GTest changes to use TEST_VM and add unmapped guard test
insights.problem: GTest test suite used TEST macro; new changes require VM-backed test harness and added a test for unmapped guarded memory verification.
insights.root_cause: GuardedMemory::verify_guards needed to handle unmapped scenarios; tests updated to validate behavior and to use VM context macros.
insights.solution: Changed several TEST to TEST_VM and added a GuardedMemory unmapped test to assert verify_guards() returns false for unmapped header.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing low-level memory verification behavior, update unit tests to run in the correct VM context and add negative tests for unmapped ranges.

insights.title: Comprehensive test for checked JNI release mismatch detection
insights.problem: Need to exercise various mismatch scenarios between different JNI allocation/releasing functions under Xcheck:jni; also earlier test caused disk full issues (addressed by toned down behavior in backport).
insights.root_cause: Lack of thorough cross-combinations test for Release* functions and array sources, and heavy test invocation permutations that could create large output.
insights.solution: Added TestCharArrayReleasing that runs native driver combinations and asserts exit codes and output messages for mismatched releases, exercising protections added in jniCheck.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding runtime checks, provide exhaustive tests covering all source/release combinations. Avoid test behavior that may produce huge outputs or disk usage; run in limited processes.

insights.title: Native test library to exercise JNI release mismatches
insights.problem: Need native code to produce arrays from different JNI sources and release them with different Release* calls to assert Xcheck:jni behavior.
insights.root_cause: Java-only tests cannot easily simulate raw malloc vs GetStringChars vs GetPrimitiveArrayCritical behaviors for release functions.
insights.solution: Added libCharArrayReleasing.c implementing Java_native testIt to create arrays from multiple sources and call release functions in different combinations to trigger error paths implemented in jniCheck.
insights.lesson_learned: Native test stubs are valuable for validating low-level JNI contract enforcement.

insights.title: Ensure read table marked clean at appropriate GC reset points
insights.problem: swap_card_tables expected the read table to be clean before swapping; previously mark_read_table_as_clean was called in entry_reset with conditional placement causing races or incorrect state for generational heaps.
insights.root_cause: mark_read_table_as_clean was called in an earlier code path not consistently for all GC entry/reset flows.
insights.solution: Moved the call to mark_read_table_as_clean into op_reset so it's executed in the common prepare/reset path (and removed duplicate earlier call).
insights.lesson_learned: Ensure card-table/read-table state transitions happen in a single canonical place to avoid missed cleanups across GC entry paths.

insights.title: Clean read table before swapping in degenerated GC path
insights.problem: swap_card_tables could be invoked without ensuring the read table is marked clean leading to crashes in GenShen during swap.
insights.root_cause: Earlier code conditioned swap solely on generation and didn't ensure read table cleanliness first.
insights.solution: Call mark_read_table_as_clean before swap_card_tables and only call swap when generation is young, reorganizing the condition structure for clarity.
insights.lesson_learned: For memory-card/remembered-set swaps, always ensure preconditions (clean read tables) before swap operations; move state-changing calls to clear places.

insights.title: Relocation size accessor must use stored size not pointer math
insights.problem: relocation_size() computed size via relocation_end()-relocation_begin() which could dereference null pointers when relocation region absent.
insights.root_cause: Pointer arithmetic on possibly-null relocation_end() caused UBSAN errors; relocation size already tracked by _relocation_size.
insights.solution: Return stored _relocation_size from relocation_size() accessor.
insights.lesson_learned: Prefer explicit size fields over computing sizes via pointer arithmetic when pointer may be null; avoid UB in size accessors.

insights.title: Remove local JfrRecorderThread class duplication and centralize in header
insights.problem: Serviceability agent could not recognize JfrRecorderThread because the thread subclass declaration was in .cpp guarded differently and not visible to vmStructs.
insights.root_cause: Thread subclass was defined locally in .cpp leading to missing declaration for vmStructs and serviceability agents.
insights.solution: Removed redundant local class in .cpp and added proper declaration in header so vmStructs and SA can see the type.
insights.lesson_learned: Type declarations used across VM introspection layers must be in headers and registered in vmStructs so SA tools can recognize thread types.

insights.title: Define JfrRecorderThread class in header and include javaThread
insights.problem: Header forward-declared JavaThread and had no concrete JfrRecorderThread subclass, causing SA to fail to map thread types.
insights.root_cause: Missing include of javaThread and missing subclass declaration led to vmStructs not being able to declare type mapping.
insights.solution: Included runtime/javaThread.hpp and added concrete JfrRecorderThread subclass with is_JfrRecorder_thread override.
insights.lesson_learned: Ensure subclass declarations for special VM threads live in headers and include required dependencies so vmStructs and SA can register them.

insights.title: Register JfrRecorderThread in vmStructs
insights.problem: Serviceability agent tests failed to recognize JfrRecorderThread because it wasn't declared in vmStructs type list.
insights.root_cause: Missing declare_type for JfrRecorderThread prevented SA from handling that thread type.
insights.solution: Added include for jfrRecorderThread.hpp and declare_type(JfrRecorderThread, JavaThread) to the vmStructs mapping.
insights.lesson_learned: Any new VM thread subclass must be registered in vmStructs for serviceability tools to be aware of it.

insights.title: Add VM_Version to toplevel VM struct listing
insights.problem: vmStructs must declare VM_Version toplevel type to allow VM_Features mapping.
insights.root_cause: New VM_Features requires VM_Version to be declared in VM struct table.
insights.solution: Added declare_toplevel_type(VM_Version) entry.
insights.lesson_learned: Update vmStructs.cpp when new toplevel VM types are introduced to keep generation consistent.

insights.title: Increase heap for test and update copyright year
insights.problem: Test used too small heap causing flakiness; also updated copyright header.
insights.root_cause: Test start config used -Xmx4m which was too constrained; update to 8m to reduce flakiness when JFR enabled.
insights.solution: Changed -Xmx4m to -Xmx8m and updated copyright.
insights.lesson_learned: Tests interacting with VM internals can be sensitive to heap size; ensure adequate headroom to avoid spurious failures.

insights.title: CharBuffer.getChars semantics corrected/documented
insights.problem: getChars(srcBegin, srcEnd, dst, dstBegin) documented as absolute indices but actually relative to position(), causing mismatch with pre-existing specification.
insights.root_cause: Method doc/impl previously used get(srcBegin, ...) rather than get(position()+srcBegin, ...). Index checks were also incorrect relative to position and limit.
insights.solution: Updated Javadoc to state relative indices and implemented Objects.checkFromToIndex(srcBegin, srcEnd, lim - pos) then call get(pos + srcBegin, ...).
insights.lesson_learned: API docs must match implementation; for relative-index overloads be explicit and validate indices relative to current position(). Use standard validation helpers.

insights.title: Add test for negative srcBegin relative to position and adjust usage
insights.problem: Existing test calls used absolute indices; new semantics are relative so tests were updated and a new negative-index test was added.
insights.root_cause: Change in getChars semantics required extending tests.
insights.solution: Added testSrcBeginIsNegationOfPosition and adjusted some calls to use 0..remaining ranges, updated expected behavior.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing API index semantics, update tests to assert both positive and negative boundary cases relative to buffer position.

insights.title: Test to ensure no bit overlays exist in ExtendedStandardFlags
insights.problem: Potential flag value collisions across Symbol kinds can cause confusing diagnostics.
insights.root_cause: Lack of test coverage validating that bits in ExtendedStandardFlags map one-to-one to single flag fields.
insights.solution: Added a reflective test that scans Flags.* and verifies each bit in ExtendedStandardFlags has exactly one corresponding static field.
insights.lesson_learned: When introducing shared bit flags, add reflection-based tests to catch accidental reuse/overlay of flag bits across different uses.

insights.title: Regression test to ensure no false 'sealed not allowed here' when flags clash
insights.problem: Previously a flag clash between 'sealed' and other internal flags produced erroneous errors.
insights.root_cause: Flag bit overlay/collision in ExtendedStandardFlags caused the parser/validator to report sealed-related errors for unrelated constructs.
insights.solution: Added a unit that exercises a mixture of constructs (RequiresIdentity annotation, WeakReference, WeakHashMap) to ensure no false sealed compile-time errors appear.
insights.lesson_learned: Add focused tests covering interactions between language features and platform/internal annotations when changing flag allocation.

insights.title: Tests for malformed @SuppressWarnings attribute handling
insights.problem: Missing tests allowed javac to crash when annotation attributes were not constants or of wrong types.
insights.root_cause: Lack of coverage for many variants of erroneous attribute forms (numeric, enum, class literal, nested arrays, etc).
insights.solution: Expanded test matrix with numerous variants and explicit expected diagnostics to ensure compiler reports errors rather than crashing.
insights.lesson_learned: Add exhaustive tests for annotation attribute resolution paths, especially when they involve constants and type conversions.

insights.title: Expose items_count_acquire for atomic reading of intern table size
insights.problem: Non-atomic access to intern table counters could lead to inconsistent behavior during CDS dumping.
insights.root_cause: Other components needed a safe way to read _items_count with acquire semantics.
insights.solution: Added declaration for items_count_acquire() to provide atomic acquire read for _items_count.
insights.lesson_learned: Expose minimal accessor functions to enforce memory ordering when multiple translation units rely on shared counters.

insights.title: Declare active task counter and wait API in CompileTask
insights.problem: No exposed API or field to support waiting for compile tasks.
insights.root_cause: Missing declaration for tracking active tasks and waiting facility.
insights.solution: Added static int _active_tasks and static wait_for_no_active_tasks() declaration.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding runtime coordination semantics, add corresponding fields and APIs to headers so other components can call into them.

insights.title: Use new lint helper when deciding to enable path linting
insights.problem: Logic used options.isExplicitlyDisabled which didn't account for the new semantics of custom lint flags.
insights.root_cause: Call sites relied on old Options API semantics.
insights.solution: Replaced with options.isLintDisabled(LintCategory.OPTIONS) to reflect new split of enable/disable checks.
insights.lesson_learned: When refactoring option-handling APIs, update all call sites to the new, clearer helpers to avoid behavioral regressions.

insights.title: Tests to exercise combinations of -Xlint options
insights.problem: Lack of tests validating the behavior when both enabling and disabling forms of -Xlint are passed.
insights.root_cause: Option precedence and combinations had minimal coverage.
insights.solution: Added a test that compiles with various -Xlint combinations and confirms expected warnings/errors.
insights.lesson_learned: Add CLI-level tests covering combinations of compiler flags when semantics are subtle.

insights.title: Documentation modernisation: use code snippets and clarify Redirect javadocs
insights.problem: Javadoc used old <pre> tags and inconsistent examples; some examples could be misread and snippet boundaries were inconsistent.
insights.root_cause: Older formatting style and inconsistent examples in the Javadocs.
insights.solution: Rewrote examples to use @snippet, clarified Redirect behavior and examples, and adjusted formatting for clarity.
insights.lesson_learned: Use modern javadoc snippet support to provide clearer, compile-friendly examples and to reduce ambiguity in API docs.

insights.title: Test that PlatformTracer class is not initialized when no filters set
insights.problem: Possible unnecessary initialization of PlatformTracer during Flight Recorder startup may incur overhead.
insights.root_cause: Previous behavior caused class initialization even when tracing filters were not set.
insights.solution: Added a test that checks Unsafe.shouldBeInitialized for PlatformTracer after stopping the initial recording to ensure it's not initialized.
insights.lesson_learned: Tests for lazy initialization should use platform primitives to detect class initialization and ensure expensive subsystems stay dormant until needed.

insights.title: Make JNI wrapper throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning null
insights.problem: JVM_CreateThreadSnapshot returned null on unsupported builds, which could lead to confusing behavior or NPEs on the Java side.
insights.root_cause: Earlier code returned nullptr under #else; Java-side contract expects an exception to signal unsupported operation.
insights.solution: Changed the return-path to THROW_NULL(vmSymbols::java_lang_UnsupportedOperationException()) when snapshot creation not supported.
insights.lesson_learned: Native JNI entrypoints should throw appropriate Java exceptions instead of returning null when operation unsupported; prefer clear error signaling for callers.

insights.title: Safely obtain JavaThread and handle virtual thread snapshot termination
insights.problem: Thread snapshot code could crash when trying to resolve a thread that had already terminated or when mapping jthread to JavaThread failed.
insights.root_cause: Code assumed JNIHandles::resolve would always return a valid oop for jthread; virtual threads special-case wasn't handled and termination could produce null OOPs.
insights.solution: Use tlh.cv_internal_thread_to_JavaThread to attempt resolution with separate java_thread and thread_oop; assert safety; detect missing java thread and return nullptr early when appropriate; compute is_virtual via java_lang_VirtualThread::is_instance and handle termination.
insights.lesson_learned: Be defensive when mapping Java-level references to VM internal structures; account for virtual threads and terminated threads and return early if snapshot isn't possible.

insights.title: Sanity test to ensure AOTCompileEagerly flag accepted and behaves
insights.problem: Need a test ensuring AOTCompileEagerly can be toggled and doesn't cause failures across training/assembly/production phases.
insights.root_cause: Flag behaviour should be validated across AOT lifecycle.
insights.solution: Added a driver test that exercises record/create/prod modes and runs with AOTCompileEagerly on/off to ensure no crashes or regressions.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing classification of VM flags, add end-to-end tests covering lifecycle modes to catch regressions.

insights.title: Optimize cbrt stub: simplify special-case checks and avoid stack spills
insights.problem: Performance regression in Math.cbrt; the generated stub did unnecessary stack stores and complex branching for NaN/Inf/zero checks.
insights.root_cause: Earlier code used stack spills and many labels for special-case handling; this caused extra memory traffic and branches.
insights.solution: Introduced ABS_MASK constant and used andpd/ucomisd checks to identify zero/NaN/Inf more directly; removed stack stack-frame use and some redundant branches to reduce instruction count and memory accesses; short-circuited denormal/Inf/NaN handling with direct comparisons.
insights.lesson_learned: When writing architecture stubs, reduce stack spills and prefer direct register/external memory comparisons using vector ops where appropriate; rework special-case handling to minimize branches.

insights.title: Ensure tests that make network calls disable system proxy selection
insights.problem: Some XML/JAXP unit tests may make network connections and be affected by system or CI proxy settings leading to flaky tests.
insights.root_cause: Tests relied on default ProxySelector which can select a proxy in CI environments or when a JVM-wide selector was configured.
insights.solution: Wrap test main with setting ProxySelector.setDefault(ProxySelector.of(null)) and restore previous selector in finally block to ensure no proxy is selected.
insights.lesson_learned: Tests making network-like calls should disable proxy selection to avoid environment-dependent failures and should restore global state afterwards.

insights.title: Disable ProxySelector for SAX catalog tests
insights.problem: Proxy selection could change behavior of SAX tests that resolve external resources.
insights.root_cause: Global proxy selector not controlled in tests.
insights.solution: Set ProxySelector.of(null) at test entry and restore previous value in finally block.
insights.lesson_learned: Reset and restore global networking state in tests that rely on direct network access or resource resolution.

insights.title: Disable ProxySelector for DTD DOM tests
insights.problem: Tests that resolve DTDs may be influenced by proxy selection and fail in some CI setups.
insights.root_cause: Global proxy selection could cause tests to reach network unexpectedly.
insights.solution: Set ProxySelector to none at test start and restore previous value in finally block.
insights.lesson_learned: Global network configuration must be controlled by tests that rely on local resources.

insights.title: Disable ProxySelector for DTD SAX tests
insights.problem: Proxy could cause flaky DTD tests.
insights.root_cause: Global proxy selector used by default.
insights.solution: Disable and restore ProxySelector at test main.
insights.lesson_learned: Tests that rely on local-only IO should ensure no proxy interference.

insights.title: Disable ProxySelector in DOMFeatureTest @BeforeClass
insights.problem: DOM feature tests could be impacted by proxy selection across VMs.
insights.root_cause: Global ProxySelector not set to null for these tests.
insights.solution: Added @BeforeClass to set ProxySelector.of(null) to prevent proxy from being used.
insights.lesson_learned: Use testing lifecycle hooks to set global state required for deterministic tests and document othervm usage when changing global selectors.

insights.title: Initialize _sampling_critical_section flag in JfrThreadLocal
insights.problem: _sampling_critical_section member was not initialized leading to potential garbage boolean state.
insights.root_cause: Constructor initializer list omitted initialization for the boolean field.
insights.solution: Added _sampling_critical_section(false) to constructor initializer list.
insights.lesson_learned: Always initialize all fields in constructor initializer lists to avoid indeterminate states for booleans or flags that gate behavior.

insights.title: Add per-thread CPU-timer and queueing state for CPU-time sampling (platform gated)
insights.problem: CPU-time sampling requires per-thread timers, an async-signal-safe queue and lock state to enqueue/dequeue CPU-time sampling requests.
insights.root_cause: New CPUTime sampling feature requires extra per-thread data structures and atomic flags to safely enqueue from signal context and dequeue in normal context.
insights.solution: Extend JfrThreadLocal with timer_t* _cpu_timer and CPUTimeLockState and associated atomic flags and queue, plus methods to manage them and lifecycle hooks (on_start/on_exit) to create/destroy timers.
insights.lesson_learned: Signal-handler driven features need careful per-thread bookkeeping and async-signal-safe queueing (SPSC) with explicit lock states; platform gating (LINUX) simplifies cross-platform builds.

insights.title: Per-thread CPU timer and async-signal-safe queue state
insights.problem: CPU-time sampling requires per-thread timers, an async-signal-safe enqueue path, and state to coordinate dequeue in non-signal contexts.
insights.root_cause: Existing JfrThreadLocal lacked storage for per-thread POSIX timer IDs, a queue for CPU-time sample requests, and lock state for safe signal vs non-signal accesses.
insights.solution: Added timer_t* _cpu_timer, CPUTimeLockState with ENQUEUE/DEQUEUE/UNLOCKED, atomic flags _has_cpu_time_jfr_requests and _do_async_processing_of_cpu_time_jfr_requests, a JfrCPUTimeTraceQueue member, and accessor/mutation functions that use atomic cmpxchg and release/acquire semantics. Also call JfrCPUTimeThreadSampling::on_javathread_create/terminate on thread life-cycle.
insights.lesson_learned: Signal-handler interaction requires minimal, async-signal-safe operations for enqueue; more complex processing must be deferred and protected by locks. Use atomic state transitions documented and tested. Thread lifecycle must register/unregister timers and queues.

insights.title: Guard walking hazard pointer list only for JavaThreads at safepoint
insights.problem: Access violation when walking thread _threads_list_ptr during thread dump because non-Java threads could be processed when not safe.
insights.root_cause: Condition allowed list walking if SafepointSynchronize::is_at_safepoint() without ensuring thread was a JavaThread; if thread wasn't JavaThread, it was unsafe to walk its list.
insights.solution: Tightened condition: only walk the list if both at safepoint and thread->is_Java_thread(), or if current thread equals the inspected thread.
insights.lesson_learned: When performing safepoint-based operations on per-thread data structures, ensure the thread kind (JavaThread) matches assumptions before walking VM-managed linked lists.

insights.title: Handle sunk stores when finishing outer strip-mined loop construction
insights.problem: Loop strip-mining expansion (outer strip-mined loop) didn't properly account for stores that were sunk out of the inner loop, leaving missing Phis or incorrect backedge inputs and potentially producing incorrect code.
insights.root_cause: The outer loop construction omitted Phis for memory slices if all inner-loop stores were sunk and didn't update backedge inputs for Phis when stores were sunk and replaced the inner phi path.
insights.solution: Added logic in OuterStripMinedLoopNode to detect sunk stores reachable from the merged memory used by the outer safepoint, create missing outer Phis for memory slices where necessary, and fix backedge inputs to point to the last sunk store in the chain. Also reorganized function names and added helper methods to encapsulate behavior.
insights.lesson_learned: When transformations move memory operations across loop boundaries (sinking), ensure outer/auxiliary loop structures are updated to preserve IR invariants—particularly Phis and memory inputs.

insights.title: Add helpers and rename sink-store related methods for clarity
insights.problem: Prior API surface for OuterStripMinedLoopNode didn't provide helper accessors or clear method names for the sunk store handling required when finishing construction.
insights.root_cause: Complexity of strip-mined outer loop finishing required clearer helper functions.
insights.solution: Added fix_sunk_stores_when_back_to_counted_loop, handle_sunk_stores_when_finishing_construction, and a few accessors for inner_counted_loop, inner_counted_loop_end, inner_loop_exit.
insights.lesson_learned: For complex compiler IR transformations, expose clear helper methods and encapsulate responsibilities; tests should cover the intricate interactions.

insights.title: Test stores sunk into outer strip-mined loop correctness
insights.problem: Compiler transformations could produce wrong results if sunk stores weren't accounted for in outer loop Phis/backedges.
insights.root_cause: Missing coverage for scenarios combining sunk stores and strip-mined loops.
insights.solution: Added a JTReg test that runs different patterns of stores (sunk/mixed) under multiple VM configs to validate correctness.
insights.lesson_learned: Add tests exercising corner-case interactions of compiler optimizations (sunk stores + strip mining) across various VM flags to detect subtle correctness regressions.

insights.title: Document multiple report-on-exit parameters
insights.problem: Man page entry for report-on-exit didn't say it could be repeated to list multiple views.
insights.root_cause: Outdated documentation string.
insights.solution: Added sentence explaining the report-on-exit parameter can be repeated to specify more than one view.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep man pages in sync with runtime option semantics; small doc tweaks reduce user confusion.

insights.title: Add @apiNote references for trim/isEmpty deprecations
insights.problem: Documentation for trim() and isEmpty() didn't point developers to newer Unicode-aware APIs (strip/isBlank/stripLeading/etc.).
insights.root_cause: Javadoc lacked guidance to newer APIs introduced in later Java versions.
insights.solution: Added @apiNote text to String.trim() and String.isEmpty() javadoc pointing to strip(), isBlank(), stripLeading(), stripTrailing().
insights.lesson_learned: API docs should guide users toward more correct or more modern alternatives; small doc changes aid migration.

insights.title: Avoid OOM on Windows by not starting many processes simultaneously
insights.problem: Test started 200 Java processes concurrently and kept Process objects, causing out-of-memory on Windows machines after prior change.
insights.root_cause: Allocating Process[] and holding references for many processes increased memory usage; Windows environment had lower capacity or different behavior.
insights.solution: Start processes one-by-one, analyze output immediately and avoid storing large arrays of Process objects.
insights.lesson_learned: Tests that spawn many processes should avoid retaining heavy resources; prefer sequential start-and-analyze to limit footprint.

insights.title: Preserve anti-dependency loads and data inputs when fixing control around barriers
insights.problem: C2 Shenandoah barrier expansion could lose anti-dependency loads and data inputs control relationships, leading to incorrect execution with Unsafe.
insights.root_cause: Existing logic in is_dominator_same_ctrl and fix_ctrl inlined expansion used ad-hoc loops and missed pushing anti-dependent loads and data inputs, causing nodes to be incorrectly moved across barriers.
insights.solution: Refactored to add helper functions: is_anti_dependent_load_at_control, maybe_push_anti_dependent_loads, push_data_inputs_at_control, collect_nodes_above_barrier; reworked fix_ctrl to use collected nodes and maintain anti-dependencies.
insights.lesson_learned: Complex graph transformations need explicit handling of anti-dependencies and control-local data flows; factor helpers and unit-test sensitive patterns.

insights.title: Expose helpers for barrier fixup
insights.problem: Header lacked declarations for newly refactored helper functions used by fix_ctrl.
insights.root_cause: Refactor in .cpp introduced new static helpers that must be declared.
insights.solution: Added declarations for collect_nodes_above_barrier, push_data_inputs_at_control, is_anti_dependent_load_at_control, maybe_push_anti_dependent_loads and adjusted fix_ctrl signature.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep header declarations consistent with implementation changes; prefer small helper functions to clarify intent.

insights.title: New test to catch lost anti-dependency loads after expansion
insights.problem: Incorrect execution with Unsafe due to lost anti-dependencies in C2/Shenandoah.
insights.root_cause: Barrier expansion could reorder memory operations leading to wrong results.
insights.solution: Added TestLostAntiDependencyAtExpansion.java to stress allocate/read/write patterns using Unsafe and validate correctness across many iterations.
insights.lesson_learned: Add targeted tests for complex GC+JIT interactions (Unsafe, barriers) to prevent regressions.

insights.title: Restore archived method handle intrinsics before finishing loading java.base
insights.problem: JVM could crash because method-handle intrinsics archived in CDS were not restored before finish_loading_javabase_classes was called.
insights.root_cause: Ordering of restore_archived_method_handle_intrinsics and AOTLinkedClassBulkLoader::finish_loading_javabase_classes was incorrect under CDS/AOT linked classes path.
insights.solution: Call SystemDictionary::restore_archived_method_handle_intrinsics() before finish_loading_javabase_classes(CHECK_JNI_ERR).
insights.lesson_learned: Initialization order matters: make sure intrinsic restoration occurs before class finalization/loading steps that expect them.

insights.title: Unix default for shouldShutdownWriteBeforeClose0
insights.problem: Platform hook needs implementation across platforms.
insights.root_cause: New Java-level hook required a C implementation on Unix too.
insights.solution: Added Java_sun_nio_ch_Net_shouldShutdownWriteBeforeClose0 returning JNI_FALSE for Unix.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding platform heuristics, provide sensible defaults on all platforms to avoid null/native resolution issues.

insights.title: Windows: shutdown write before close hook returns true
insights.problem: Windows requires different closing semantics to avoid peer resets when threads are blocked in read.
insights.root_cause: No hook value defined; Windows must indicate shutdown-before-close behavior.
insights.solution: Implemented Java_sun_nio_ch_Net_shouldShutdownWriteBeforeClose0 to return JNI_TRUE on Windows.
insights.lesson_learned: Native platform differences must be reflected via small native hooks; tests should validate cross-platform behavior.

insights.title: Test for graceful EOF when closing while peer reads
insights.problem: Regression where closing a socket/channel while another thread is blocked reading produced connection reset instead of EOF.
insights.root_cause: Platform close semantics differed; no test verified behavior for both platform and virtual threads.
insights.solution: Added parameterized JUnit test covering platform and virtual threads, checks that peer sees EOF and that blocked thread receives appropriate exception.
insights.lesson_learned: Add platform-sensitive tests for low-level I/O behaviors, exercise both virtual and platform threads.

insights.title: Implement cmov for ge/gt float comparisons on RISC-V
insights.problem: C2 generated asserts/ShouldNotReachHere for BoolTest::ge and BoolTest::gt in enc_cmove_cmp_fp leading to crashes.
insights.root_cause: enc_cmove_cmp_fp previously asserted instead of routing ge/gt cases to appropriate cmov implementations.
insights.solution: Call newly implemented cmov_cmp_fp_ge and cmov_cmp_fp_gt for ge/gt cases; implemented the functions with proper EVEX-like flow for single/double and fallthrough semantics.
insights.lesson_learned: Ensure all BoolTest branches are implemented; assertions that assume canonicalization may be invalid after upstream changes.

insights.title: Declare incompressible scope around fill_words/zero_memory loops
insights.problem: Loops that emit fixed-size instruction sequences could be compressed when RVC applied, changing expected instruction sizes and breaking runtime assumptions.
insights.root_cause: Previously no explicit incompressible scope around code emission loops; compression could alter layout used by later patching or expected fixed-length sequences.
insights.solution: Wrap critical loops in IncompressibleScope instances to guarantee fixed-length emission for patching and alignment.
insights.lesson_learned: When emitting instruction sequences that will be patched or relied upon for fixed length, declare incompressible scopes to prevent RVC from changing layout.

insights.title: Route BoolTest::ge/gt to implemented cmov functions
insights.problem: enc_cmove_cmp_fp had unreachable assertions for BoolTest::ge and BoolTest::gt.
insights.root_cause: Previous code assumed canonicalization would route these cases elsewhere; that assumption broke and led to crashes.
insights.solution: Replace assertions with calls to cmov_cmp_fp_ge and cmov_cmp_fp_gt.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid ShouldNotReachHere() in code paths that may be affected by transforms; implement conservative handling.

insights.title: Declare new cmov comparison helpers
insights.problem: New cmov helpers for ge/gt needed header declarations.
insights.root_cause: Implementation added functions but header lacked their prototypes.
insights.solution: Added declarations for cmov_cmp_fp_ge and cmov_cmp_fp_gt.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep headers in sync with implementation when extending assembler helpers.

insights.title: IPR tests for FP comparison cmov on RISC-V
insights.problem: Need to exercise and verify that C2 emits correct cmov/compare FP sequences including ge/gt variants.
insights.root_cause: New code paths for ge/gt require verification on RISC-V.
insights.solution: Added/updated TestFPComparison2.java to validate code generation and avoid regressions.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing backend instruction generation, add targeted architecture-specific tests.
constructs: test harness and multiple test cases (file contains many test classes)

insights.title: Add Sectigo TLS root (E46)
insights.problem: New Sectigo roots were not present in cacerts bundle.
insights.root_cause: Root CA additions are ongoing updates to trusted store.
insights.solution: Added PEM entry for Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root E46 to cacerts data files.
insights.lesson_learned: Updating root stores requires checksum/test updates to VerifyCACerts to maintain reproducible images.

insights.title: Add Sectigo TLS root (R46)
insights.problem: New Sectigo roots were not present in cacerts bundle.
insights.root_cause: Root CA additions are ongoing updates to trusted store.
insights.solution: Added PEM entry for Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root R46 to cacerts data files.
insights.lesson_learned: Root additions require updating verification tests and checksums.

insights.title: Add Sectigo Code Signing root (E46)
insights.problem: New Sectigo code signing roots missing.
insights.root_cause: CA rotation/updates require adding new roots to cacerts.
insights.solution: Added PEM entry for Sectigo Public Code Signing Root E46.
insights.lesson_learned: CA store updates must be accompanied by test updates and checksum updates.

insights.title: Add Sectigo Code Signing root (R46)
insights.problem: New Sectigo code signing roots missing.
insights.root_cause: CA rotation/updates require adding new roots to cacerts.
insights.solution: Added PEM entry for Sectigo Public Code Signing Root R46.
insights.lesson_learned: CA store updates must be accompanied by test updates and checksum updates.

insights.title: Add interop test cases for new Sectigo roots
insights.problem: Tests must exercise new root names/URLs for interoperability verification.
insights.root_cause: New roots added to cacerts need to be validated by test harness.
insights.solution: Added test metadata and URL mappings for sectigotlsrootr46 and sectigotlsroote46.
insights.lesson_learned: When modifying trust stores, update test harness data and manual-run instructions for interop tests.

insights.title: Google CAInterop test URL hostnames wrong for demosite
insights.problem: Several test CA URLs pointed to 'demo.pki.goog' which caused Google CAInterop tests to fail against the expected test hosts.
insights.root_cause: Hard-coded test URLs used an incorrect host domain (demo.pki.goog) that did not match the actual test endpoints (demosite.pki.goog).
insights.solution: Update the hostnames in CATestURLs to use 'demosite.pki.goog' for the affected CA aliases.
insights.lesson_learned: Hard-coded external test endpoints are brittle — prefer a single configuration point or documented constants for test endpoints and validate them when upstream test infrastructure changes.

insights.title: Add tests for Sectigo code signing root CAs
insights.problem: Need test coverage for new code-signing roots (R46/E46) including revoked/valid paths.
insights.root_cause: New CA entries require interop and revocation checks.
insights.solution: Added a comprehensive test class encoding intermediate/valid/revoked certificates and exercising ValidatePathWithParams with CRL/OCSP.
insights.lesson_learned: Include both positive and negative (revoked) checks when adding new roots; embed DER/PEM payloads carefully in test sources.

insights.title: Update expected cacerts checksum and add new cert fingerprints
insights.problem: cacerts bundle changed due to added roots; tests must reflect new count and checksum.
insights.root_cause: Added 4 new certificates increased COUNT and changed CHECKSUM.
insights.solution: Updated COUNT, CHECKSUM and added fingerprint entries for new Sectigo roots.
insights.lesson_learned: Bundle changes must be tracked in verification tests to ensure CI detects unintended modifications.

insights.title: Avoid configure --help error messages by exporting ECHO
insights.problem: Running configure --help produced error messages after an autoconf change due to missing ECHO environment variable for the generated script call.
insights.root_cause: Previously the generated script was invoked with PRINTF but not ECHO defined, causing some platforms to error.
insights.solution: Pass ECHO=echo into the subshell invocation invoking the generated script.
insights.lesson_learned: When invoking generated scripts in subshells, ensure all expected environment utilities are provided to avoid confusing errors on edge platforms.

insights.title: Kill LVN effects when encountering NewInstance of class with class initializer
insights.problem: Static initializer side effects were not considered when doing local value numbering for NewInstance: a field load could be incorrectly optimized away leading to incorrect program behavior.
insights.root_cause: LVN optimization didn't consult whether the NewInstance referred to a class with a class initializer that has side effects.
insights.solution: Extended do_NewInstance to query ciInstanceKlass::has_class_initializer and call kill_memory() if necessary (when class not initialized and either not loaded or has class initializer).
insights.lesson_learned: Compiler IR optimizations must be conservative about class initialization side effects; query class metadata to avoid removing observable side-effecting operations.

insights.title: Expose has_class_initializer
insights.problem: Caller needed to detect whether instanceKlass had a class initializer to decide optimizations.
insights.root_cause: No existing ci wrapper for class_initializer check.
insights.solution: Added ciInstanceKlass::has_class_initializer() delegating to get_instanceKlass()->class_initializer().
insights.lesson_learned: Provide safe VM-entry wrappers for class metadata queries used by optimization passes.

insights.title: Declare has_class_initializer on ciInstanceKlass
insights.problem: Header needed declaration for the newly added method.
insights.root_cause: Implementation added method; header needed update.
insights.solution: Added declaration bool has_class_initializer();
insights.lesson_learned: When adding VM-entry methods, update headers consistently.

insights.title: Test static initializer side effects not elided by C1 optimizations
insights.problem: C1 JIT could remove class-initializer side effects under LVN and cause observable differences.
insights.root_cause: Value numbering removed loads before class initializer ran.
insights.solution: Added a test that forces -Xcomp and checks that class initializer side effects are respected (throws if optimization removed side effects).
insights.lesson_learned: Add focused tests for compiler static-init ordering and side effects; use -Xcomp to trigger first-time-only initializers.

insights.title: Add nesting checks before grow operations to avoid arena reallocation corruption
insights.problem: MStack::push and other push/grow routines could cause reallocation without performing nesting checks, leading to memory corruption.
insights.root_cause: The code previously invoked grow() unconditionally (which may reallocate arena memory) without calling _nesting.check(...) to ensure arena safety.
insights.solution: Added maybe_grow() wrappers that call _nesting.check(_a) before grow and switched push() to call maybe_grow(); added similar checks in Node_Array::maybe_grow.
insights.lesson_learned: When using arena allocators with potential reallocation, always perform safety checks before operations that may reallocate; centralize checks into maybe_* helpers.

insights.title: Remove redundant nesting checks in grow paths and rely on maybe_grow
insights.problem: Redundant or misplaced nesting.check calls caused inconsistencies; grow semantics standardized to assume maybe_grow was called.
insights.root_cause: Checks existed in multiple places leading to incorrect invariants and possible corruption.
insights.solution: Removed direct _nesting.check(_a) calls from grow implementations; rely on callers using maybe_grow().
insights.lesson_learned: Centralize reallocation-safety checks to avoid missed checks and duplication; ensure all callers use safe helpers.

insights.title: Add maybe_grow wrapper for Block_Array to do nesting checks
insights.problem: map() used grow() directly which could reallocate without nesting checks.
insights.root_cause: Direct grow() call omitted nesting safety check.
insights.solution: Added maybe_grow() that performs _nesting.check(_arena) and uses grow(i) only when needed; changed map() to call maybe_grow().
insights.lesson_learned: Operations that mutate arrays should use safe growth helpers that perform allocator safety checks.

insights.title: Assert growth preconditions in Block_Array::grow
insights.problem: grow() expected to be called only when expansion needed but had previous redundant checks.
insights.root_cause: Unclear contract between maybe_grow() and grow().
insights.solution: Changed grow() to assert that i >= Max() and removed the earlier nesting.check and early return; rely on maybe_grow to do safety checks.
insights.lesson_learned: Clearly separate precondition checks (maybe_grow) and raw operations (grow) to keep invariants clear and maintainable.

insights.title: Fuzz/driver test for OptoNodeListSize VM flag
insights.problem: Regression or memory corruption could be triggered by varying -XX:OptoNodeListSize without a test harness.
insights.root_cause: Node stack size/growth issues needed stress testing for different sizes.
insights.solution: Added a driver test that runs a child JVM with a random OptoNodeListSize and verifies no crash; uses -Xcomp to exercise compiler paths.
insights.lesson_learned: Add randomized driver tests for VM tuning knobs that can trigger allocation/growth edge cases.

insights.title: Avoid system proxy interference in delayed URL parsing tests
insights.problem: Test intermittently failed because system proxy selection caused connections to fail (403 or other unexpected codes) when URL parsing was delayed.
insights.root_cause: System ProxySelector could select a proxy and affect connections started in delayed parsing mode.
insights.solution: When delayed parsing is enabled, set ProxySelector.setDefault(...) to return Proxy.NO_PROXY so tests open direct connections.
insights.lesson_learned: Network tests should force deterministic proxy behavior to avoid test flakiness caused by environment proxy settings.

insights.title: Avoid system proxies interfering with expect-continue test
insights.problem: Test failed with 403 due to system proxy being used for URL.openConnection().
insights.root_cause: openConnection() used system proxy by default leading to unexpected server responses.
insights.solution: Call url.openConnection(Proxy.NO_PROXY) to force direct connection in test.
insights.lesson_learned: Network tests should avoid relying on system proxy configuration; explicitly choose NO_PROXY where appropriate.

insights.title: Reduce per-test heap and require machine memory for compact GC tests
insights.problem: Several vmTestbase/compact tests timed out on large-memory machines where default heaps were too large causing long GC pauses/timeouts.
insights.root_cause: Test assumed smaller runtime memory; on huge-memory machines default Xmx may be very large causing tests to run longer.
insights.solution: Added @requires os.maxMemory > 3G and supply -Xmx2G for the run invocation to limit test heap and make runtime deterministic.
insights.lesson_learned: On tests sensitive to heap sizes and GC behavior, explicitly set Xmx and require machine memory bounds to avoid environmental flakiness.

insights.title: Same heap constraints added to NonbranchyTree compact test
insights.problem: See Compact_InternedStrings above; required similar adjustment.
insights.root_cause: Same as above.
insights.solution: Added @requires os.maxMemory > 3G and -Xmx2G.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep test-suite configurations consistent across related tests.

insights.title: Same heap constraints added to Strings ArrayOf compact test
insights.problem: See Compact_InternedStrings above; required similar adjustment.
insights.root_cause: Same as above.
insights.solution: Added @requires os.maxMemory > 3G and -Xmx2G.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep test-suite configurations consistent across related tests.

insights.title: Same heap constraints added to Humongous InternedStrings compact test
insights.problem: See Compact_InternedStrings above; required similar adjustment.
insights.root_cause: Same as above.
insights.solution: Added @requires os.maxMemory > 3G and -Xmx2G.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep test-suite configurations consistent across related tests.

insights.title: Different error output when running under virtual thread test factory
insights.problem: Test expected a 'Main method not found' message, but when run with TEST_THREAD_FACTORY=Virtual the runtime prints a NoSuchMethodException with a different message.
insights.root_cause: Virtual thread test harness changes how the main method error is surfaced (NoSuchMethodException) versus the classic message used by the test.
insights.solution: Make the test accept both outcomes by checking if the pb.command() contains test.thread.factory=Virtual and assert the corresponding message accordingly.
insights.lesson_learned: Tests that assert exact error messages can be brittle when test harness or runtime mode changes. Prefer recognizing modes or checking exception types rather than fragile full-message matching.

insights.title: Provide rotate and multi-xor helpers for SHA3 GPR implementation
insights.problem: SHA3 GPR implementation needs small bit-manipulation helpers (rotate, rax1, eor3) used in the keccak round implementation.
insights.root_cause: Existing assembler lacked convenience helpers used by the new GPR-based SHA3 intrinsic implementation.
insights.solution: Add rolw/rol, rax1, eor3 helper methods and expose some Assembler methods via using declarations.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding complex instruction sequences it's helpful to encapsulate repeated instruction patterns in assembler helper methods to keep implementation readable and reduce mistakes.

insights.title: Add GPR-based SHA3 (keccak) intrinsic implementation
insights.problem: SHA3 intrinsics previously assumed SIMD availability; on systems without SIMD a fallback was needed. Also frame/register use must respect reserved registers and frame-pointer usage.
insights.root_cause: Lack of a non-SIMD implementation for SHA3 resulted in missing intrinsic support on systems without SIMD or when SIMD is disabled.
insights.solution: Implement generate_sha3_implCompress_gpr and related keccak_round_gpr which implement SHA3 using general-purpose registers (GPR). Wire selection logic so the GPR implementation is used when SIMD is disabled (UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic false) while SIMD implementation remains available.
insights.lesson_learned: Provide alternate code paths for different CPU capabilities and guard runtime selection with capability flags. Keep register usage explicit and provide code paths that save/restore registers or use the frame pointer if required.

insights.title: Test updates to run SHA3 intrinsic tests with new flag
insights.problem: The new UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic flag must be ignored by older JVMs / test runners; tests need to include IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions or ensure the right flags are present.
insights.root_cause: New VM option added; tests that pass the option must be robust against older VMs or be consistent with the implementation selection.
insights.solution: Add -XX:+IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions -XX:+UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic in comments and define multi-invocation runs exercising both UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic and -UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic variants for verification.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding new VM options, make tests tolerant to the presence/absence of these options by using IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions and explicitly exercising both configurations.

insights.title: Multi-block SHA3 tests updated for UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic combinations
insights.problem: Need to ensure multi-block intrinsic tests exercise both SIMD and non-SIMD variants and that the test harness tolerates unrecognized options.
insights.root_cause: New flag UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic changes which implementation is used; tests must be explicit and tolerant to VM options.
insights.solution: Add -XX:+IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions and run test permutations with -UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic and +UseSIMDForSHA3Intrinsic and preserve frame pointer variants.
insights.lesson_learned: Test permutations should cover different implementation modes introduced by new flags and be tolerant to unknown options for forward/backward compatibility.
constructs: JTReg run configurations (comments and run directives)

insights.title: Adapt benchmarks to new JFR event API (offer) and throttle default
insights.problem: JFR event sampling API changed: code previously computed duration and called emit() conditionally; new pattern is offer(...) which computes duration and may commit (throttled). Also StartFlightRecording benchmarks must disable throttle for micro-bench reproducibility.
insights.root_cause: JFR sampling changes replaced shouldCommit/emit pattern with offer() helpers and introduced throttle default behavior that can suppress events.
insights.solution: Replace manual timestamp/duration/emit logic with SocketWriteEvent.offer/SocketReadEvent.offer calls. Add jdk.SocketWrite#throttle=off / jdk.SocketRead#throttle=off to JFR start options to ensure events are not rate-limited during the benchmark.
insights.lesson_learned: When framework APIs centralize decision logic (throttling/thresholds), call the framework 'offer' helper instead of duplicating timestamp/duration checks; tests/benchmarks should explicitly disable throttling when precise event emission is required.

insights.title: doccheck test metadata updated to include new bug id and minor fixes
insights.problem: Test did not report missing man page files because the link checker missed certain missing-file cases.
insights.root_cause: LinkChecker previously didn't log missing file references at the point of checking path existence.
insights.solution: Add bug id to test header and rely on updated LinkChecker/FileProcessor changes to detect missing files.
insights.lesson_learned: Tests that exercise file-system links must defensively check for file existence and report failures early; keep test metadata in sync when tests are expanded.

insights.title: Use diamond operator and modernize SimpleFileVisitor signature
insights.problem: Older explicit generic type declarations and checked IOException signatures were unnecessary and made code verbose.
insights.root_cause: Minor modernization to match newer Java language conveniences.
insights.solution: Use Files.walkFileTree with new SimpleFileVisitor<>() diamond and remove throws IOException from visitFile/postVisitDirectory overrides where not needed.
insights.lesson_learned: Modernize test utilities incrementally; prefer concise generics and avoid redundant checked exceptions in lambda/visitor overrides when safe.

insights.title: Better error accounting and explicit missing file logging
insights.problem: LinkChecker.isOK used separate counters (duplicateIds, missingIds, missingFiles, badSchemes) and returned false only if all zero; missingFiles not always incremented or logged properly.
insights.root_cause: Inconsistent error recording and poor message aggregation made it hard to discover missing man page files.
insights.solution: Use log.noErrors() and track missingFiles++ when id not found; on close() report errors and throw a concise RuntimeException. When a referenced file path doesn't exist, log a missing file reference immediately and return.
insights.lesson_learned: Prefer a single source of truth (log.noErrors()) for pass/fail status in checkers and ensure missing-file conditions are logged and counted at the earliest detection point.

insights.title: Restore rbcp (bcp) in throw_exception template to handle deoptimized frames
insights.problem: Cooperative sampling and JVMTI PopFrame exposed a scenario where the interpreter's bcp (rbcp) might not be restored after deoptimization, causing inconsistent frame state during popframe handling.
insights.root_cause: Throw exception entry sequence didn't restore bcp which could lead to inconsistent interpreter frame information after returning from a deoptimized frame.
insights.solution: Add __ restore_bcp() in generate_throw_exception() to ensure rbcp is restored before setting popframe_processing bit.
insights.lesson_learned: Low-level interpreter template changes must account for deoptimization paths; restoring interpreter context (bcp) is critical when frames can be deoptimized before exception handling or popframe operations.

insights.title: Restore rbcp in throw_exception for RISC-V interpreter
insights.problem: Same interpreter frame inconsistency for RISC-V as other ports.
insights.root_cause: Missing restore_bcp in template led to inconsistent frames when handling PopFrame after deoptimization.
insights.solution: Call __ restore_bcp() in the throw_exception template.
insights.lesson_learned: Interpreter templates should be kept semantically consistent across ports; small omissions replicate bugs across architectures.

insights.title: Restore rbcp in x86 throw_exception template
insights.problem: Same as other ports: missing restore leads to inconsistent interpreter frames during JVMTI PopFrame operations.
insights.root_cause: Omission of restore_bcp in interpreter throw path.
insights.solution: Insert __ restore_bcp() to ensure consistent interpreter state.
insights.lesson_learned: Cross-platform interpreter fixes should be applied to all architecture templates.

insights.title: Improve pattern for extracting hex narrow_oop_base
insights.problem: Regex expected decimal digits but log uses hex addresses; pattern failed to parse narrow_oop_base in logs.
insights.root_cause: Regex used (\d+) when log prints hex digits (0-9a-fA-F).
insights.solution: Change regex to use [0-9a-fA-F]+ for the hex address.
insights.lesson_learned: When parsing logs that include addresses, prefer hex-aware regexes. Tests that parse logs must align with the output format.

insights.title: Add tests for preview and malformed class file versions to prevent javap crashes
insights.problem: Javap crashed on preview/minor versions; need coverage to avoid regressions.
insights.root_cause: Lack of tests exercising class files with unusual minor/major combos and misplaced flags.
insights.solution: Introduce a parameterized JUnit test that generates class files with different major/minor combinations including preview minor and malformed access flags and asserts javap does not crash and reports expected errors.
insights.lesson_learned: When making tool fixes, add unit tests that create boundary/preview cases programmatically to prevent regressions.

insights.title: Verify invokespecial to interface method properly (resolve target and detect interface)
