insights.problem: Illegal invokespecial to interface methods (indirect interface or unrelated) were not reliably detected by the verifier because assignability checks didn't indicate whether the resolved target was an interface.
insights.root_cause: resolve_and_check_assignability used context/klass inconsistently and did not report whether the target was an interface to the caller, leading to missing verification failure for interface-method invokespecial cases.
insights.solution: Refactor resolve_and_check_assignability to accept current_klass and target_name/from_name and return a target_is_interface out-parameter; update is_reference_assignable_from calls to pass a pointer for target interface detection and call path accordingly.
insights.lesson_learned: Verification logic that relies on class resolution and assignability must propagate type-kind (interface vs class) information back to callers; small mismatches in resolver context (current vs target) can create subtle verification holes.

insights.title: Update verificationType header to support interface detection path
insights.problem: Header signatures needed to change to propagate interface detection to verifier.
insights.root_cause: resolve_and_check_assignability semantics changed to accept/return interface boolean.
insights.solution: Update declarations accordingly and add helper overloads that preserve previous callers.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing core verification semantics, update headers and provide compatibility overloads to avoid widespread changes.

insights.title: Catch illegal invokespecial to interface methods (indirect or unrelated) during verification
insights.problem: invokespecial targeting an interface method in an indirect superinterface wasn't flagged correctly; verifier didn't emit the precise error and could allow invalid bytecode.
insights.root_cause: Verification relied on assignability that treated interfaces like Object in some branches; needed to detect whether the resolved target was an interface and reject it explicitly for invokespecial.
insights.solution: Refactor the invokespecial verification branch to call is_reference_assignable_from with an out-parameter that indicates whether the target is an interface, reject cases where it is an interface (even if assignable by treating it as Object), and improve error messages.
insights.lesson_learned: Verification must distinguish interface vs class semantics even when assignability maps interfaces to Object for some checks; method-invocation bytecodes have distinct constraints that require explicit interface detection.

insights.title: Improve link-time resolution error message for invokespecial interface misuse
insights.problem: At link-time, invokespecial to an interface method that is not in a direct superinterface should be rejected; message previously said 'indirect superinterface' in a way that could be misleading.
insights.root_cause: The check allowed certain indirect interface cases to reach link-time and used an awkward message.
insights.solution: Ensure the check enforces 'direct superinterface' requirement and produce clearer error message 'is not in a direct superinterface of ...'.
insights.lesson_learned: Both verifier and link-resolver need consistent checks and consistent, clear error messages for the same classfile validation rules.

insights.title: New tests to ensure invokespecial to interface methods are rejected by verifier and by runtime linking
insights.problem: Verification/linker previously allowed or mis-reported illegal invokespecial usage for interface methods; need tests covering both verified and unverified modes.
insights.root_cause: Lack of tests that assert the exact failure mode under verified and unverified (link-time) configurations.
insights.solution: Add JTReg tests and small .jasm files that provoke invokespecial to interface method cases and assert VerifyError messages in verified mode and IncompatibleClassChangeError messages in unverified mode.
insights.lesson_learned: Bytecode edge cases should have both verification and link-time tests; ensure messages are matched (or at least contain expected substrings) rather than relying on exact formatting when possible.

insights.title: Make invokeAny null TimeUnit test less brittle
insights.problem: Test asserted exact NullPointerException message which changed after a prior JDK change (message text differs because it's coming from another implementation), causing spurious failures.
insights.root_cause: Implementation detail changed upstream (invokeAny delegated) so message text differed; test relied on exact message match.
insights.solution: Remove the assertion on the exact message and only check the exception type.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid asserting exact exception messages in compatibility tests when message originates from another API/implementation boundary; prefer asserting exception class or behavior.

insights.title: Event throttler gets an extra disabled CPU-time throttler and mapping for CPUTimeSample
insights.problem: CPU time sampling integration requires a default (disabled) throttler to be present for the CPUTimeSample event.
insights.root_cause: When adding CPU-time sampling feature, the throttler registry needed to be extended to include a (disabled) CPUTime sample throttler.
insights.solution: Create _disabled_cpu_time_sample_throttler in create() and return it in for_event when requested; ensure destroy() frees it.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding new event types, update central registries and factory methods so new types have consistent throttler/manager objects; ensure creation and destruction are balanced.

insights.title: Add disabled throttler for CPUTimeSample event
insights.problem: Event throttler lookup didn't handle CPUTimeSample event ID and there was no disabled throttler placeholder.
insights.root_cause: New CPU time sampler introduced a new event id; throttler factory asserted only known event ids.
insights.solution: Added _disabled_cpu_time_sample_throttler initialized as disabled and returned for JfrCPUTimeSampleEvent; adjusted assertions.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding a new event type, update central registries (throttler factory) and consider adding sentinel/disabled instances for events that default to disabled.

insights.title: Ensure has_sample_request accounts CPU-time JFR requests
insights.problem: Jfr::has_sample_request() initially returned true only if JfrThreadLocal::has_sample_request was set; CPU-time sampling added additional pending requests which must be considered.
insights.root_cause: New CPU-time sampling feature added has_cpu_time_jfr_requests; inline helper needed to reflect both kinds of requests.
insights.solution: Change has_sample_request to inspect the JfrThreadLocal and return true if either has_sample_request() or has_cpu_time_jfr_requests() is set.
insights.lesson_learned: Inline helpers used by hot paths must be updated when new thread-local request kinds are introduced to ensure sampling threads pick them up.

insights.title: JFR sampling: account for CPU-time specific requests
insights.problem: Existing Jfr::has_sample_request only checked general sample requests, not CPU-time specific sampling requests.
insights.root_cause: CPU-time sampler introduces a second kind of per-thread JFR request; older check missed them, causing CPU-time sampling to be ignored in some code paths.
insights.solution: Updated Jfr::has_sample_request to consult JfrThreadLocal::has_cpu_time_jfr_requests() in addition to the existing request check.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding a new request/flag state, ensure all convenience predicates and 'has X' checks are updated so new behavior is visible across code.

insights.title: Expose current signal handler retrieval
insights.problem: No helper to query the existing signal handler for a given signal from code that can't/shouldn't set a handler.
insights.root_cause: Code that needs to introspect a signal handler previously had to reimplement sigaction logic or rely on global state.
insights.solution: Added PosixSignals::get_signal_handler_for_signal(int) which performs sigaction(NULL, &oact) and returns the handler via get_signal_handler(&oact).
insights.lesson_learned: Encapsulate platform queries behind helper methods; avoid duplicating sigaction usage (and potential subtle differences) across the codebase.

insights.title: Allow sampling when thread is native
insights.problem: JFR sample builder asserted that the JavaThread was in Java state only; CPU-time sampling may occur when thread is in native state.
insights.root_cause: Previously an assert enforced jt->thread_state() == _thread_in_Java; CPU-time sampling can happen in native code and must be supported.
insights.solution: Relaxed the assert to accept _thread_in_native as well and added build_cpu_time_sample_request which constructs a request from ucontext; introduced a biased-sample marker by clearing pc/bcp.
insights.lesson_learned: Profile/sampling code must tolerate native-thread states; assertions that assume Java-only states can break new sampling mechanisms.

insights.title: Process CPU-time enqueued requests path
insights.problem: Thread sampling path did not know how to drain and process CPU-time sampling requests queued asynchronously by signal handlers.
insights.root_cause: CPU-time sampling uses signal handlers and an async-safe enqueue path; the existing drain_enqueued_requests handled only method-sampling requests.
insights.solution: Added record_cpu_time_thread helper, drain_enqueued_cpu_time_requests, drain_all_enqueued_requests and process_cpu_time_request entrypoint; compute_top_frame got an extra biased flag; CPU-time queue is handled with locks and can send lost-samples events.
insights.lesson_learned: Asynchronous signal-driven sampling requires carefully designed enqueue/dequeue protocols (signal-safe enqueue, locked dequeue) and dedicated draining code on the mutator/sampler thread; tests should validate lost-sample accounting and biased samples.

insights.title: Register CPU-time thread sampling component in JfrRecorder
insights.problem: New CPU-time sampling component needed to be constructed and destroyed with other JFR components.
insights.root_cause: JfrRecorder create/destroy lifecycle only managed a thread sampler and event throttler, not the CPU-time sampler.
insights.solution: Added JfrCPUTimeThreadSampling creation/destruction in JfrRecorder::create_components and destroy_components and a create_cpu_time_thread_sampling helper.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding a subsystem component, ensure it's integrated into the global recorder lifecycle so resources are allocated and freed deterministically.

insights.title: CPU-time sampling subsystem (Linux implementation)
insights.problem: Enable JFR CPU-Time profiling via a new sampler that works with per-thread timers, signal handlers and an async-signal-safe queue.
insights.root_cause: JEP 509 requires capturing CPU-time-based profiling samples; this must interact with signals and per-thread POSIX timers.
insights.solution: Added header declaring JfrCPUTimeSampleRequest, a fixed-size signal-safe SPSC queue, JfrCPUTimeThreadSampling class with create/destroy, rate control, on_javathread_create/terminate hooks, and functions to send events/lost sample reports.
insights.lesson_learned: Platform-specific implementations (Linux) must be guarded and provide a fallback no-op implementation on other platforms; signal-safety and careful queue sizing (resize_for_period) are critical.

insights.title: Added CPUTimeSample and CPUTimeSamplesLost events metadata
insights.problem: New CPU-time sampling events need metadata for JFR tooling and UI.
insights.root_cause: New event types must be declared in metadata so tools can parse and render them.
insights.solution: Appended <Event name="CPUTimeSample"> and <Event name="CPUTimeSamplesLost"> entries with fields description and throttle attributes.
insights.lesson_learned: Metadata updates are necessary alongside runtime changes for new event types to be usable by tooling; ensure throttle settings and field types are accurate.

insights.title: Handle MethodCounters metadata backlinks in finalize_oop_references
insights.problem: finalize_oop_references traversed metadata that could be MethodData, Method, etc. After changes, MethodCounters objects were used with backlinks to Method and were not handled leading to incorrect casts or missed metadata processing.
insights.root_cause: Introduction of MethodCounters as a separate Metadata type (after JDK-8355003) left some code paths that inspect metadata without checking for methodCounters type.
insights.solution: Added checks for is_methodCounters and correct extraction ((MethodCounters*)m)->method() in finalize_oop_references and nmethod CheckClass, and a new virtual is_methodCounters() in metadata.hpp.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding new subclassed metadata kinds, audit all metadata traversal sites for proper instanceof/is_xxx checks; missing checks cause mis-classification and latent bugs.

insights.title: Expose is_methodCounters() virtual
insights.problem: New metadata variant MethodCounters needed type predicate support.
insights.root_cause: Other code relies on is_methodData and similar predicates; the new kind must be discoverable.
insights.solution: Added virtual bool is_methodCounters() const { return false; } to Metadata base class.
insights.lesson_learned: Adding a new subclassed type typically requires a corresponding virtual predicate to aid runtime identification across the codebase.

insights.title: Avoid race by waiting for VMStart event before adding listener
insights.problem: Test sometimes failed on macOS due to race with adding listener before VMStart event arrived; debuggee would be resumed unexpectedly.
insights.root_cause: Test added listener before waiting for VMStart; if VMStart arrives while adding, debuggee resumed incorrectly.
insights.solution: Reordered: connect, waitForVMStart(), then addListener to avoid resuming the debuggee prematurely.
insights.lesson_learned: Test harnesses interacting with VM events must ensure ordering: wait for VMStart before registering listeners that affect resum/stop behavior.

insights.title: Fix incorrect conditional register encoding for cmov variants
insights.problem: Incorrect operands passed to cmov/conditional move encodings (used wrong source operand) led to incorrect codegen and failing FP comparison tests.
insights.root_cause: Pattern matching in instruction definitions produced wrong operand order for cmov encoding variants (APX vs non-APX special-cases), leading to incorrect codegen for certain floating-point comparisons.
insights.solution: Adjusted match/format/ins_encode bodies to use the correct source operand and added TEMP effects where appropriate.
insights.lesson_learned: Assembler pattern definitions are sensitive to operand order; small typos in ad files can change generated machine code semantics and break floating-point comparisons/tests.

insights.title: Avoid asserts when VerifyStack encounters unreachable bytecodes after returns/gotos
insights.problem: C2 asserted on usage of unreachable basicblock/bytecodes (assert(bb->is_reachable())) during VerifyStack/deopt when bytecodes following return/goto were present in unreachable blocks.
insights.root_cause: VerifyStack was not accounting for bytecodes that don't fall through (gotos, returns, throws, jsr/ret, switch) and treated later bytecodes as reachable incorrectly.
insights.solution: Added falls_through(Bytecodes::Code) helper enumerating bytecodes that don't fall through; updated code to consult falls_through and added jtreg tests (TestVerifyStackWithUnreachableBytecode.java and its .jasm) to exercise scenarios.
insights.lesson_learned: Bytecode semantics (fall-through vs not) must be honored when reconstructing control flow for stack verification and deoptimization. Add small helpers for maintainability and comprehensive tests for edge combinations.

insights.title: More informative IOExceptions for spawn-helper failures
insights.problem: When spawn helper (jspawnhelper) failed (e.g., mismatch, terminated), the thrown IOException lacked actionable information making diagnosis hard.
insights.root_cause: Generic throwIOException created short messages lacking context about spawn helper internal failures and didn't vary message by launch mode.
insights.solution: Refactored throwIOExceptionImpl to include externalDetail, internalDetail and formatted errno text; introduced throwInternalIOException that appends SPAWN_HELPER_INTERNAL_ERROR_MSG for posix_spawn mode and propagate mode to throwExitCause; updated callers to call throwInternalIOException for spawn-helper related errors.
insights.lesson_learned: Provide actionable, mode-aware error messages for low-level platform helpers; consider distinguishing internal helper failures vs normal errno-based failures; tests should verify message content.

insights.title: Detect spawn-helper internal failure messages in tests
insights.problem: Tests could report spawn helper internal failures indistinguishably as unexpected IOExceptions.
insights.root_cause: New, longer error messages were introduced by ProcessImpl to help debugging; tests should treat these messages as failures rather than OK patterns.
insights.solution: Updated Basic.java to include SPAWNHELPER_FAILURE_MSG pattern and fail tests if messages contain "Possible reasons:".
insights.lesson_learned: When error messages are improved to be more informative, tests comparing message contents should be updated to detect and treat these new messages as intended failures (or handle them gracefully).

insights.title: Document thread-safety semantics of ZipCoder and expose charset
insights.problem: ZipCoder instances for non-UTF8 charsets were not thread-safe and earlier implementation didn't make the charset accessible to the ZipFile Source caching logic.
insights.root_cause: ZipCoder held CharsetDecoder/Encoder state which is not thread-safe for non-UTF8 encoders; ZipFile.Source cache keyed did not include charset leading to different ZipFile instances incorrectly sharing a parsed central directory interpreted with wrong charset.
insights.solution: Added ZipCoder.charset() accessor, documented thread-safety, and used per-ZipFile ZipCoder instances; adjusted callers to pass ZipCoder through and to compute entry-specific ZipCoder via zipCoderFor(cen, pos, fallback).
insights.lesson_learned: When caching file-parsed structures across instances, include all parameters that influence parsing (e.g., charset). Make thread-safety of decoder/encoder explicit and avoid sharing non-thread-safe resources across threads.

insights.title: ZipFile Source cache must include charset & per-entry UTF-8 flag handling
insights.problem: When multiple ZipFile instances for the same file were created using different Charsets, the cached parsed ZIP structure could be used with the wrong charset and decode entry names incorrectly.
insights.root_cause: Source key used for caching the parsed central directory omitted the Charset; additionally, entries can set a per-entry UTF-8 flag which should override the fallback ZipCoder.
insights.solution: Key now records the charset used when constructing ZipFile; Source.get and constructor accept a ZipCoder; added zipCoderFor(cen,pos,fallback) that returns UTF8 ZipCoder when entry flag uses UTF-8; updated methods (getEntry, getInputStream, getEntryName, getZipEntry) to pass zipCoder; added Source internals to use supplied ZipCoder when parsing and validating entry comments; added two tests ZipFileCharsetTest and ZipFileSharedSourceTest.
insights.lesson_learned: Cache keys must include all inputs that affect parsing semantics (including Charset). Respect per-entry flags (e.g., USE_UTF8) when decoding names. Tests should cover concurrent/multi-instance usage with different charsets.

insights.title: Verify cached Source uses correct Charset
insights.problem: Regression where Source cache could be parsed with wrong Charset if different ZipFile instances used different charsets.
insights.root_cause: Cache missing charset key and per-entry UTF-8 override not considered.
insights.solution: Test constructs a ZIP with ISO-8859-15 encoded name and opens two ZipFile instances (one with incorrect ISO-8859-1, one with correct ISO-8859-15) while both are open to assert entries are resolved only by correct charset.
insights.lesson_learned: Unit tests should reproduce real-world cross-instance usage, e.g., open multiple ZipFile instances with different settings while cache is active.

insights.title: Adapt key derivation to KDF API; ensure zeroing of intermediate secrets
insights.problem: Legacy HKDF usage and API mismatch across TLSv1.2/1.3 paths; risk of leaked SecretKeySpec objects.
insights.root_cause: Old HKDF helper had extract/expand calls; transition to KDF requires different call patterns and parameter specs.
insights.solution: Switched to javax.crypto.KDF with HKDFParameterSpec for extract/expand semantics; unified deriveKey(type) API usage; added KeyUtil.destroySecretKeys in finally blocks to clear preMasterSecret/saltSecret etc.
insights.lesson_learned: Centralize KDF usage in SSL code to avoid duplication and ensure secrets are cleared. Tests referencing removed HKDF helper were removed/updated.

insights.title: Add Power9/Power10 VSX opcodes and support for vector load/store variations
insights.problem: C2 needed non-volatile vector registers available for register allocation and codegen must support newer VSX instruction encodings and alignments.
insights.root_cause: Vector register encoding and instruction variants differ across Power architectures; previous code only supported older encodings.
insights.solution: Added new opcodes and inline functions for lxvx/stxvx/lxvp/stxvp, aligned addressing helpers, and helper vsrtp/vsrsp for Power10.
insights.lesson_learned: Porting/optimizing for newer ISAs requires carefully adding instruction encodings and alignment helpers; maintainability improved by grouping architecture-specific paths.

insights.title: Unified non-volatile register save/restore with vector register support and alignment
insights.problem: Multiple places duplicated logic to save/restore GPR/FPR/VSR; for Power9/10 vector regs need special alignment and different store instructions per architecture.
insights.root_cause: Previous code used static spill_nonvolatiles layout and per-site ad-hoc code. Newer architectures use different vector instructions (stxvp/stxv/stxvd2x).
insights.solution: Introduced save_nonvolatile_registers/restore_nonvolatile_registers with include_fp_regs and include_vector_regs flags and save_nonvolatile_registers_size() helper. Use PowerArchitecturePPC64 checks to choose correct instructions, adjust offsets and alignment accordingly.
insights.lesson_learned: Centralize register save/restore logic with capability flags for architecture features; always compute sizes with alignment and assert consistency to prevent frame-layout bugs.

insights.title: Optimize multidimensional array allocations and reuse patterns
insights.problem: Many multi-dimensional int/boolean arrays were allocated using new int[a][b] which can be less efficient; code used many temporary arrays.
insights.root_cause: Java JVM allocation overhead for many nested arrays can be significant in crypto operations; repeated allocations in hot loops degrade performance.
insights.solution: Introduced integerMatrixAlloc and booleanMatrixAlloc factory helpers that allocate the first dimension and then initialize second-dimension slices in a loop; replaced many new int[...][][] with these helpers; avoided unnecessary NTT inverse calls commented out.
insights.lesson_learned: For performance-sensitive code, manual array allocation patterns and reuse reduce GC pressure and improve performance; provide small helper factories to clarify intent.

insights.title: Respect TypeProfileCasts flag when emitting profiling for casts
insights.problem: C1 emitted profiling info for instanceof/checkcast/array-store even when TypeProfileCasts JVM flag was disabled, leading to unnecessary profiling hooks and possible overhead.
insights.root_cause: Code only checked profiled_method != nullptr and not the global flag TypeProfileCasts.
insights.solution: Added TypeProfileCasts flag check in conditions that set profiled_method/profiled_bci on LIR type checks.
insights.lesson_learned: Feature-gating flags must be consulted where behavior is emitted; adding a new profiling mode requires auditing all emit sites.

insights.title: Eliminate races with available() by caching available counts and adding under-construction sentinel
insights.problem: Observers could read inconsistent capacity/used and compute available() concurrently with free set rebuilds; some calls could see an intermediate state and assert.
insights.root_cause: available() was computed on-the-fly as capacity - used without a lock; free set rebuilds mutate capacity/used and observers could race.
insights.solution: Introduced explicit _available[] array to be updated under the heap lock in the same critical sections that change capacity/used; added FreeSetUnderConstruction sentinel; provided available_in() (locked) and available_in_not_locked() (unlocked, with debug assertions acquiring lock to validate) and changed callers to use available_in_not_locked() for non-locked reads; add asserts in caller code to ensure not reading sentinel at runtime.
insights.lesson_learned: For values that are observed concurrently, maintain an explicit atomic/locked copy and update it atomically-within-critical-section to avoid read-time recomputation races. Provide debug checks to catch races early.

insights.title: Introduce FreeSetUnderConstruction sentinel and available cache
insights.problem: Same as above: need to track available atomically and detect under-construction states.
insights.root_cause: available previously derived on-demand, causing races.
insights.solution: Add _available[] and FreeSetUnderConstruction constant and methods to manage it.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding cached derived fields, ensure they are updated in lock-holding paths and expose both locked and unlocked accessors with clear semantics.

insights.title: Return generational transfer result and log when appropriate
insights.problem: phase5_epilog performed generation balancing and logging inline; callers sometimes needed result info for generational heap mode.
insights.root_cause: Phase epilog logic needed to expose results to callers for logging in some modes.
insights.solution: Changed phase5_epilog to return ShenandoahGenerationalHeap::TransferResult and adjusted caller to log result when generational mode is active.
insights.lesson_learned: When refactoring GC phases, surface useful results instead of hiding them; makes diagnostic logging and subsequent processing simpler.

insights.title: Report available memory limited by collector reserve correctly
insights.problem: available() reported free_set->available() directly, which could differ from what mutators can use due to collector reserves.
insights.root_cause: Failure to account for collector reserved bytes vs mutator visibility.
insights.solution: Compute available via generation::available() and min with free_set()->available(), ensuring reported available matches mutator-usable amount.
insights.lesson_learned: When reporting available memory to other subsystems, ensure semantics match consumers' expectations (mutator vs collector view).

insights.title: EagerJVMCI default semantics and delayed exit behavior
insights.problem: Changing default for EagerJVMCI and behavior when compiler unavailable could cause early VM exit on non-JIT threads.
insights.root_cause: Eager initialization of JVMCI may occur on non-Compiler threads; earlier code immediately exited on missing compiler. With EagerJVMCI default true (when UseJVMCICompiler true), we must not exit from non-compiler threads during initialization path that may not request compilation.
insights.solution: Change HotSpotJVMCICompilerConfig.DummyCompilerFactory: check EagerJVMCI flag and if runtime.getCompilerToVM().isCompilerThread() throw noCompilerError(), otherwise delay throwing until a compilation request is actually made (compileMethod now throws noCompilerError()). Also set EagerJVMCI default to true (conditional flag behavior in jvmci_globals.hpp).
insights.lesson_learned: Flag defaults that change initialization behavior must be coordinated with runtime checks to avoid exiting from threads that won't request the component; delay fatal errors until the first use when safer.

insights.title: Pass tree to resolveSelf to support receiver parameter in constructor local classes
insights.problem: Receiver-parameter constructor syntax (Local(Class this)) failed with a wrongly-reported early reference error.
insights.root_cause: resolveSelf previously accepted a Name argument without the tree context; the early-reference check needed the field-access tree to detect receiver parameter usage.
insights.solution: Changed resolveSelf signature to accept JCFieldAccess tree instead of Name and forwarded tree to rs.resolveSelf; added special-case check isReceiverParameter to permit early reference when the field access is a constructor receiver parameter.
insights.lesson_learned: Name-only overloads lose syntactic context needed for certain early-construction checks; retain AST node when decisions depend on lexical form (e.g., receiver parameter in constructor).

insights.title: Allow receiver parameter constructor local-class syntax in early construction context
insights.problem: Javac rejected local-class constructors that use a receiver parameter when invoked during early construction checks.
insights.root_cause: Attr/Resolve early-reference checks flagged receiver-parameter constructor param as RefBeforeCtorCalled unless specially recognized.
insights.solution: Added isReceiverParameter helper and updated resolveSelf to bypass the early-reference check for receiver-parameter occurrences (tree==method.recvparam.nameexpr).
insights.lesson_learned: Language changes that introduce new syntactic forms (receiver params in constructors) require small but precise changes in semantic checks that consider AST-node identity rather than just names.

insights.title: Add unsignedMultiplyExact and powExact family (signed/unsigned) methods
insights.problem: No built-in exact unsigned multiply/power operations that throw on overflow for integral types.
insights.root_cause: Developers commonly need exact arithmetic with overflow detection for unsigned semantics; no standard helpers existed.
insights.solution: Added unsignedMultiplyExact(int,int), unsignedMultiplyExact(long,int), unsignedMultiplyExact(long,long), powExact(int,int), unsignedPowExact(int,int), powExact(long,int), unsignedPowExact(long,int) to Math and mirrored in StrictMath. Implemented with wide intermediate arithmetic and overflow checks; provided unit tests (IntegralPowTest).
insights.lesson_learned: Introducing new exact arithmetic operations requires careful overflow semantics for unsigned vs signed, wide intermediates, using existing multiplyExact helpers when possible; provide comprehensive tests across ranges and edge cases.

insights.title: Documentation and minor API clarifications for StableValue
insights.problem: Post-integration comments highlighted small documentation inaccuracies and missing exception notes (e.g. recursive set detection) and phrasing issues.
insights.root_cause: Docs and Javadoc wording did not fully capture reentrancy/recursive-set behavior and some param descriptions were ambiguous.
insights.solution: Updated Javadoc comments (orElseSet, setOrThrow, supplier() and function() param docs) and small wording fixes throughout StableValue.java.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep API docs precise about concurrency and reentrancy semantics; document recursive set behaviors explicitly.

insights.title: Rename of content field access and wrapper method to clarify semantics
insights.problem: Confusing naming of unsafe offset constant and accessors (CONTENT_OFFSET, wrappedContentAcquire) risked misunderstanding and incorrect reads/writes.
insights.root_cause: Naming inconsistency between a field named contents and methods/offset constants using singular 'content' led to potential confusion and maintainability issues.
insights.solution: Renamed CONTENT_OFFSET to CONTENTS_OFFSET and wrappedContentAcquire() to wrappedContentsAcquire(); updated all call sites and wrapAndSet generic signature to use T newValue.
insights.lesson_learned: Use consistent naming for underlying fields and unsafe accessors; renaming small internals can avoid subtle bugs and improve code readability.

insights.title: Stable collections construction and view semantics
insights.problem: Returning pre-built serializable empty collections for stable, lazy collections would expose Serializable semantics and break contract (stable lists/maps are not Serializable).
insights.root_cause: Previously code returned List.of() or Map.of() for empty stable collections; those are Serializable and therefore leak incorrect guarantees.
insights.solution: Always construct StableList/StableMap objects even for size==0 to preserve non-Serializable stable semantics and add helper interface HasStableDelegates to expose internal delegates for view implementations.
insights.lesson_learned: Be careful when returning shared empty immutable collections — they may have implicit interfaces (like Serializable) that violate new type contracts.

insights.title: Use wrappedContentsAcquire when rendering stable values
insights.problem: StableUtil.renderElements/renderMappings used wrappedContentAcquire(), inconsistent with renamed accessor.
insights.root_cause: Renamed accessor in StableValueImpl required corresponding updates in StableUtil to avoid referencing stale method name.
insights.solution: Updated renderElements/renderMappings to call wrappedContentsAcquire() and corrected string concatenation order.
insights.lesson_learned: When renaming low-level accessors ensure all render/debug helpers are updated to avoid reflection of stale state or compilation errors.

insights.title: Added tests for view stability and lazy evaluation
insights.problem: Post-integration comments required more coverage for compositions of views and ensuring they remain lazy (unevaluated) and handle nulls correctly.
insights.root_cause: Complex interactions of subList(), reversed(), and other view operations were not fully exercised.
insights.solution: Added tests viewsStable, childObjectOpsLazy, indexOfNullInViews, sublistReversedToString and utilities for composing view operations.
insights.lesson_learned: Complex view composition requires combinatorial tests to catch regressions in laziness and structural invariants.

insights.title: Added stable entry and iteration tests
insights.problem: Need to validate Map.Entry implementations for lazy evaluation and equals/hashCode semantics.
insights.root_cause: New StableMap entry wrapper semantics required tests ensuring toString(), equals, and hashCode behave correctly before/after evaluation.
insights.solution: Added stableEntry and stableForEachEntry tests exercising lazy value read and toString/equality behavior.
insights.lesson_learned: When wrapping values lazily in collections, add tests for Map.Entry contract (equals/hashCode/toString) and for interaction with iterators and forEachRemaining.

insights.title: Move metadata printing logic out of PrettyWriter
insights.problem: PrettyWriter contained both event printing and metadata printing responsibilities.
insights.root_cause: Single class handled two distinct concerns: pretty printing of events and metadata formatting.
insights.solution: Introduce MetadataWriter to handle metadata printing; Metadata now instantiates MetadataWriter and delegates printType/flush.
insights.lesson_learned: Separate formatting concerns to reduce coupling and improve maintainability; move metadata-specific logic into a dedicated class.

insights.title: New MetadataWriter for event metadata formatting
insights.problem: Need a focused implementation to print JFR metadata in a human-readable format.
insights.root_cause: PrettyWriter's responsibilities were split to simplify event printing vs metadata printing.
insights.solution: Added MetadataWriter that extends StructuredWriter and encapsulates metadata printing: printType, printField, annotations handling, id comments and formatting helpers.
insights.lesson_learned: Encapsulate domain-specific formatting in dedicated classes; helps review and testability.

insights.title: Create ephemeral UnixDomainSocketAddress provider with safe close semantics
insights.problem: Benchmarks used a global temp directory and generated socket Paths in a non-thread-safe manner; getPath()/cleanup could throw after socket closed.
insights.root_cause: Static tempDir and incrementing counter introduced races and lifetime issues; Path could be invalid when socket closed.
insights.solution: Bind ServerSocketChannel with null (let system pick address), record the UnixDomainSocketAddress path immediately after bind (sscFilePath), and clean up that path during teardown. Simplified family param handling.
insights.lesson_learned: When creating ephemeral domain sockets, record platform-assigned addresses immediately and clean them up deterministically; avoid shared mutable temp globals in benchmarks.

insights.title: Record UDS file path immediately after bind and delete safely
insights.problem: Test created UDS file using createTempDirectory then bind; later getPath() could fail if socket closed or file removed unexpectedly.
insights.root_cause: Socket address lifecycle not captured at bind time; earlier code computed path later leading to potential exceptions.
insights.solution: Capture ssc.getLocalAddress() and its getPath() right after bind and use sscFilePath for teardown deletion.
insights.lesson_learned: Capture OS-assigned resources at bind/creation time to ensure correct cleanup, especially in benchmarks/tests.

insights.title: Rename uabs helpers to g_uabs to avoid glibc symbol collision
insights.problem: glibc 2.42 introduced uabs() symbol causing name collision and build failures.
insights.root_cause: Global helper function named uabs conflicts with a symbol in the system C library.
insights.solution: Rename uabs variants to g_uabs and add appropriate wrappers for overloads; update all call sites to g_uabs.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid using short, generic names in widely included headers; prefer project-specific prefixes to avoid collisions with platform headers.

insights.title: Improve lazy initialization of available currencies set
insights.problem: Synchronized lazy initialization used a single mutable static field and locked on access; potential contention and late initialization issues.
insights.root_cause: Classic double-checked/synchronized lazy pattern adds contention and complexity.
insights.solution: Use StableValue.supplier to hold a supplier that constructs a HashSet lazily (computeAllCurrencies) and replace getCurrencies with computeAllCurrencies; available is now a Supplier<HashSet<Currency>>.
insights.lesson_learned: Use stable/lazy helper utilities (StableValue) to replace ad-hoc synchronized lazy init for lower contention and clearer semantics.

insights.title: Handle supplementary characters in character literals
insights.problem: A char literal containing a supplementary code point (two UTF-16 code units) was being accepted incorrectly for non-string char literals.
insights.root_cause: Tokenizer didn't reject supplementary code points for char literals (only for strings) and could mis-handle multi-surrogate sequences in char literals.
insights.solution: When scanning a char literal (not a string), if the code point is not BMP, lexError with IllegalCharLiteralMultipleSurrogates; added diagnostic and tests.
insights.lesson_learned: Character literal scanning must enforce BMP-only semantics per Java spec; include tests for multi-surrogate literals.

insights.title: Add diagnostic message for multiple-surrogate char literal
insights.problem: Compiler diagnostics lacked a message key describing multiple-surrogate char literal errors.
insights.root_cause: New lexical error case required a specific diagnostics key and message.
insights.solution: Add compiler.err.illegal.char.literal.multiple.surrogates message to compiler.properties.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding new lexer errors, add resource diagnostic keys and example tests to ensure regression coverage.

insights.title: New test to ensure P11Mac can be initialized with unknown-key-algorithm SecretKey
insights.problem: Regression potential where Mac.init(secretKey) would throw for keys whose algorithm name is unrecognized but whose material is usable.
insights.root_cause: Earlier P11SecretKeyFactory algorithm checks could reject valid usage for Mac services.
insights.solution: Added test initializing Mac instances for various HmacSHA* algorithms with a SecretKeySpec using algorithm "Any"; asserts no exception is thrown.
insights.lesson_learned: Add focused tests for cryptographic initialization edge cases where algorithm names are not strict indicators of suitability.

insights.title: Introduce CompressibleScope/IncompressibleScope abstraction and rename flags
insights.problem: Assembler scopes for compressible/incompressible regions used inconsistent naming and required refined scoping to avoid instruction compression issues in some assembler routines.
insights.root_cause: Existing Region naming and boolean field in_compressible_region needed clearer semantics (scope) and consistent use across codebase.
insights.solution: Rename Incompressible/CompressibleRegion to Scope variants, rename internal flags to in_compressible_scope and update constructors/destructors accordingly; use scope objects in many call sites.
insights.lesson_learned: Clear naming (Scope vs Region) and RAII-style scope objects reduce confusion and make localized compression control safer.

insights.title: Deprecate getPermission() (Security Manager removal)
insights.problem: Legacy URL.getPermission and related network permission classes are obsolete as Security Manager is removed.
insights.root_cause: Security Manager deprecation and removal made permission-based access control irrelevant.
insights.solution: Annotate getPermission() with @Deprecated(since = "25", forRemoval = true) and add @SuppressWarnings("removal") where necessary.
insights.lesson_learned: When platform-level features are removed, mark related APIs deprecated for removal and annotate call sites/tests to avoid noisy warnings.

insights.title: Deprecate getPermission() in URLConnection
insights.problem: Permission checks as part of URLConnection are no longer meaningful without Security Manager.
insights.root_cause: Security Manager no longer supported; permission objects cannot control resource access in practice.
insights.solution: Mark getPermission() as @Deprecated(since = "25", forRemoval = true) with suppression of removal warnings.
insights.lesson_learned: API deprecations should clearly annotate replacement guidance and reason (removed feature).

insights.title: Deprecate NetPermission class for removal
insights.problem: Network permission classes are obsolete post Security Manager removal.
insights.root_cause: Permissions cannot be used for access control when the Security Manager is removed.
insights.solution: Mark class deprecated with @Deprecated(since = "25", forRemoval = true) and update javadoc.
insights.lesson_learned: Deprecate and annotate security-related classes when their fundamental platform mechanism is removed.

insights.title: Remove NetPermission reference for UnixDomainSockets
insights.problem: Code had a static NetPermission that is now deprecated and unnecessary.
insights.root_cause: Permissions are being deprecated; keeping permission objects in code increases churn and warnings.
insights.solution: Removed NetPermission field and rely on other means; ensured isSupported() returns static supported flag.
insights.lesson_learned: When platform-level security primitives are removed, remove auxiliary permission constructs from lower-level APIs as well.

insights.title: Rename set_flags to set_has_appendix and clarify bit handling
insights.problem: set_flags used a compact bit-setting approach that risked confusing which bits were preserved and may be error-prone.
insights.root_cause: Old implementation used bit arithmetic assumptions and did not use explicit masks per-shift making maintenance harder.
insights.solution: Rename method to set_has_appendix, use explicit shifts and masks (set_has_appendix sets only its bit and preserves others), and use resolution_failed_shift constant in set_resolution_failed.
insights.lesson_learned: When manipulating bitfields, prefer explicit masks and named shifts to make intent clear and avoid accidental clobbering of other flag bits.

insights.title: Increase allowed node growth per IGVN iteration
insights.problem: An assert triggered due to excessive live node increase in a single IGVN iteration for certain workloads.
insights.root_cause: Threshold for per-iteration live-node increase was too low for some code patterns causing assert failures.
insights.solution: Increase max_live_nodes_increase_per_iteration multiplier from NodeLimitFudgeFactor * 2 to * 3.
insights.lesson_learned: Static safety margins may need tuning as optimizations evolve; prefer adaptive bounds or document why thresholds are chosen.

insights.title: Optimize ObjectMonitor::exit to favor fast succession
insights.problem: Releasing a monitor did not always hand off to an entry_list successor fast-path, causing extra work and wake-ups.
insights.root_cause: Exit path always dropped and reacquired lock in ways that didn't special-case presence of a successor; logic scattered and repeated.
insights.solution: Short-circuit check: if no successor and entry_list non-empty, find tail and call exit_epilog directly; reworked comments and flow to reduce unnecessary reacquire loops.
insights.lesson_learned: Prioritize quickly handing off locks to waiting successors to reduce wake contention; document tricky waitset/entry_list race scenarios thoroughly.

insights.title: Limit shrink of archive regions to not drop below -Xms
insights.problem: Deallocating CDS archive regions could shrink the heap below MinHeapSize (-Xms) or grow/shrink heap incorrectly.
insights.root_cause: Shrinking logic did not cap the number of regions to shrink based on MinHeapSize; could uncommit too many regions.
insights.solution: Compute max_shrink_count based on capacity - MinHeapSize and only call _hrm.shrink_at up to that cap, otherwise insert into free list; improved logging.
insights.lesson_learned: When shrinking memory, enforce global lower bounds such as -Xms to avoid violating JVM heap invariants.

insights.title: Adapter for system-call-style MethodHandles capturing errno
insights.problem: System-call-style foreign method handles return negative values and capture errno in a capture-state MemorySegment. There was no shared, performant helper to adapt such handles into a caller-friendly API.
insights.root_cause: No internal adapter existed to consistently extract a captured error state (e.g. errno) and present a simple (int|long) result convention where negative indicates error encoded as -errno.
insights.solution: Added CaptureStateUtil with a shared CAPTURE_LAYOUT, pooled Arena allocation, cached MethodHandles for extraction/guards, and adaptSystemCall() that composes MHs for try/finally arena management and error extraction.
insights.lesson_learned: Use pooling and stable cached MethodHandles for composition-heavy APIs to avoid repeated combinator inflation and to enable early initialization-safe use. Validate MH signatures early and provide platform-appropriate capture-state layout lookups.

insights.title: Avoid combinator re-creation via StableValue caches
insights.problem: Composing method handles for every adapted target would allocate many temporary combinators and hurt performance.
insights.root_cause: No reuse of common basic combinators for extraction/guards.
insights.solution: Introduce StableValue-based caches (SEGMENT_EXTRACTION_HANDLE_CACHE, HANDLES_CACHE) and reusable MethodHandles for guards and cleanup.
insights.lesson_learned: Cache MethodHandle building blocks in static stable structures when they are reused across many adapters.

insights.title: Unit tests for CaptureStateUtil behavior
insights.problem: CaptureStateUtil behaviour must be validated for successful and error return paths and argument validation.
insights.root_cause: New adapter handles many corner cases (return type, first arg MemorySegment, unknown capture name) and needs tests.
insights.solution: Added tests that exercise int/long success and error and assertion tests for invalid inputs.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding method-handle-based utilities, include tests that cover type invariants and negative paths to ensure clear error messages.

insights.title: Microbenchmarks for CaptureStateUtil
insights.problem: Need to measure overhead of adapted system-call handles vs explicit allocation.
insights.root_cause: Potential performance regression when using thread-local arena allocations vs explicit arena.
insights.solution: Added JMH microbench to compare explicit allocation and adapted (thread-local) allocation for success and failure cases.
insights.lesson_learned: Benchmarks help verify the cost of abstraction and pooling strategies; include both success and failure paths.

insights.title: Introduce ReverseBytesNode base class
insights.problem: ReverseBytesINode/ReverseBytesLNode/etc duplicated similar behavior.
insights.root_cause: Each ReverseBytes* subclass inherited InvolutionNode but needed a shared Value() implementation.
insights.solution: Add ReverseBytesNode subclass of InvolutionNode and make specific ReverseBytes types derive from it.
insights.lesson_learned: When multiple nodes share semantics, factor a common subclass so Value()/helper logic can be centralized.

insights.title: Optimize small-array fill stub on RISC-V
insights.problem: Array fill stub used less-optimal sequences for small counts (<8 bytes) and duplicated code paths, causing inefficiencies.
insights.root_cause: Previous implementation performed stores/branching and had duplicated checks; used increment/decrement idioms and fallthrough labels inconsistently.
insights.solution: Refactored logic: early branch for short arrays, simplified shift/slli usage, reorganized small-count handling with clear exit label and explicit loops for bytes/shorts, eliminating duplicated code and improving clarity.
insights.lesson_learned: Simplify and centralize small-size handling in stubs and avoid duplicated instructions; prefer clear labels and unified exit points for maintainability.

insights.title: Honor annotation default value when absent in class file
insights.problem: @Registered (and other) annotation default values were ignored if the annotation had no elements stored in the classfile (element list empty).
insights.root_cause: has_annotation() inspected annotation elements and returned false when element list was empty but a default exists.
insights.solution: Add default_value parameter to has_annotation/annotation_value and return default when element-value pair is empty.
insights.lesson_learned: Annotation default values are not stored in classfile element lists; classfile processing must explicitly handle empty element lists and propagate declared defaults.

insights.title: Test overriding of annotations respecting defaults
insights.problem: Needed a regression test to ensure default annotation values are respected and can be overridden.
insights.root_cause: JFR class inspector previously ignored defaults; test ensures behavior.
insights.solution: Add test that defines @Enabled/@Registered in super/child classes and verifies commit results using JFR Recording.
insights.lesson_learned: When fixing annotation parsing, add end-to-end tests that exercise the higher-level behavior (commit/record) as well as the low-level parsing.

insights.title: Always create archive files with write permission in output mode
insights.problem: When creating CDS/AOT archives in read-only/dump mode, file permissions were set to read-only (0444) unless dumping static archive flag set, causing failures for subsequent processes expecting writable files.
insights.root_cause: Mode decision used 0444 vs 0666 based on CDSConfig::is_dumping_preimage_static_archive(); but in output open_as_output() the file should be created writable for other processes.
insights.solution: Always use 0666 when creating the output archive file.
insights.lesson_learned: File creation mode should be chosen to allow expected subsequent access; prefer permissive creation and then restrict if necessary.

insights.title: Allow VM_Version::VM_Features to be mapped by JVMCI
insights.problem: JVMCI config reader needs to support fields with type VM_Version::VM_Features and the bitmap offsets.
insights.root_cause: New VM_Features is a toplevel struct requiring special handling when reading VM fields.
insights.solution: Treat "VM_Version::VM_Features" as a valid field type in the configuration reader.
insights.lesson_learned: Native-to-Java struct mapping code must be updated when new native types are introduced into VM structs.

insights.title: Expose VM_Features bitmap fields to JVMCI VM structs
insights.problem: JVMCI needs access to VM_Version::_features VM_Features and _features_bitmap[0] offsets.
insights.root_cause: VM_Features is a new layout; vmStructs declarations must include its fields.
insights.solution: Added static_field and nonstatic_field entries for VM_Version::VM_Features and _features_bitmap[0], and added VM_LONG_CPU_FEATURE_CONSTANTS macro expansion.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing in-VM structures, update all vmStructs generation locations (JVMCI, SA, etc.) to maintain tooling compatibility.

insights.title: Remove old feature name insertion helper
insights.problem: Old helper assumed single 64-bit feature mask; with bitmap migration it's removed.
insights.root_cause: Feature representation changed to VM_Features bitmap.
insights.solution: Deleted insert_features_names implementation that iterated a 64-bit mask.
insights.lesson_learned: When migrating data representation, remove/replace helpers that assumed older layouts.

insights.title: Expose features_string and remove old features() API
insights.problem: Old features() returned uint64_t but new representation uses VM_Features; API updated to hide raw bitmap.
insights.root_cause: VM_Features migration changed how features are exposed.
insights.solution: Removed static uint64_t features() and old insert_features_names declaration, retained features_string accessor.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep stable high-level APIs (features_string) and change low-level internals when migrating representations.

insights.title: Expose new AVX10 CPUFeature enum values
insights.problem: Java-side CPUFeature enum needed to be updated to include AVX10 features for JVMCI mapping.
insights.root_cause: Native side introduced AVX10 flags; JVMCI enums must match.
insights.solution: Added AVX10_1 and AVX10_2 enum values.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding platform features, ensure Java-side enums used by tooling mirror native constants.

insights.title: Convert VM feature bitmap to EnumSet with a generic converter
insights.problem: JVMCI needs to convert the VM feature bitmap (possibly multi-word) to EnumSet of CPUFeature enums.
insights.root_cause: VM_Features is a bitmap; mapping requires computing element index and bit mask.
insights.solution: Added convertFeatures() helper that reads constants entries (VM_Version::CPU_* mapping to bit indices) and tests corresponding bits in the VM_Features backing memory using Unsafe.
insights.lesson_learned: Provide robust conversion utilities for native-to-Java feature bitmaps and document expected layout (element size, offsets).

insights.title: Use features bitmap address and size to convert features
insights.problem: Earlier conversion assumed compact single-value; now need address+offset+size.
insights.root_cause: VM_Version::_features moved to struct and bitmap is array; JVMCI must add offset into base address.
insights.solution: Compute featuresBitMapAddress using vmVersionFeatures + vmFeaturesFeaturesOffset and pass size to convertFeatures.
insights.lesson_learned: When reading in-VM memory with Unsafe, combine base address and field offsets consistently and provide size checks.

insights.title: Expose addresses/offsets for VM_Features to JVMCI
insights.problem: Need to expose VM_Version::_features address and bitmap offset and size so JVMCI can read bits.
insights.root_cause: VM_Features is a native struct and its internal layout must be accessible.
insights.solution: Added vmVersionFeatures address, vmFeaturesFeaturesOffset, and vmFeaturesFeaturesSize fields by reading field addresses/offsets from VMStructs.
insights.lesson_learned: Expose both base addresses and offsets/size when sharing native structures across language boundaries.

insights.title: Adjust expected long constant outputs for new feature encoding
insights.problem: Tests expecting raw long constant values for CPU feature constants must be updated because constant semantics changed (value now index instead of bitmask).
insights.root_cause: Feature constants are now indices, not bitmasks, causing expected numbers to change.
insights.solution: Updated expected sample values in test comments and check values.
insights.lesson_learned: Low-level tests that assert exact constant numeric values must be updated when representation switches from mask to index/bitmap.

insights.title: Include new AVX10 features in CPU list test
insights.problem: CPUInfoTest needs to expect new feature names in the list.
insights.root_cause: Native feature additions (AVX10_1/AVX10_2) require tests updated to include those names.
insights.solution: Added avx10_1 and avx10_2 to expected feature list and bumped copyright year.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep tests in sync with platform feature additions.

insights.title: Make test feature-agnostic when needing preview minor version
insights.problem: Test relied on using a preview API to get preview minor version in the compiled class, which makes test fragile when APIs change.
insights.root_cause: Using a concrete preview API in the test couples the test to that API's preview state.
insights.solution: Use ByteCodeLoader to create a PreviewClass with explicit preview minor version, making test independent of actual preview APIs present.
insights.lesson_learned: When tests require specific classfile minor versions (preview), generate bytecode explicitly rather than relying on language/SDK preview features that may change.

insights.title: Add coderFromChar and putCharsAt helpers and remove fillNull
insights.problem: StringLatin1 lacked some low-level helpers needed by AbstractStringBuilder improvements; fillNull removed to avoid redundant array fills.
insights.root_cause: StringBuilder robustness refactor required utilities to compute coder and efficient char writes.
insights.solution: Added coderFromChar(), putCharsAt overloads for 4 and 5 chars, and removed fillNull.
insights.lesson_learned: Low-level string compact representations benefit from small helper routines to centralize bounds-checks and encoding logic.

insights.title: Adjust putCharsAt semantics and remove fillNull
insights.problem: Various helpers used different incrementing idioms; make putCharsAt write by absolute indices for clarity and safety.
insights.root_cause: Previous implementations used post-incremented indices and returned end index; callers were refactored to not need returned end.
insights.solution: Change putCharsAt to void and write characters at explicit offsets, remove fillNull.
insights.lesson_learned: Prefer clearer index arithmetic (explicit indices) in low-level byte/char store helpers to avoid off-by-one mistakes and make callers simpler.

insights.title: Update test patch to new putCharsAt signature
insights.problem: Test helper used old putCharsAt signatures returning int; signature changed to void.
insights.root_cause: StringUTF16.putCharsAt signature changed.
insights.solution: Update helper to call new void methods and bump copyright.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing low-level APIs, update test harness patches accordingly.

insights.title: Add more CompactStringBuilder tests including replace growth cases
insights.problem: StringBuilder robustness changes need expanded test coverage to catch capacity/expansion corner cases.
insights.root_cause: Refactor to improve robustness required additional tests (e.g., replace that forces expansion) and test permutations of latin1/utf16 inputs.
insights.solution: Added tests covering append with arrays, replace growing capacity cases, and additional run configurations (Xcomp).
insights.lesson_learned: Complex mutable string manipulations need combinatorial tests for compact/utf16 modes and capacity growth points.

insights.title: Add test to exercise near-Integer.MAX_VALUE capacities
insights.problem: StringBuilder capacity growth logic near Integer.MAX_VALUE must be safe in both compact and non-compact modes.
insights.root_cause: Previous tests didn't fully exercise 'huge plus' paths for both encodings.
insights.solution: Added testHugePlus to append extremely large sequences in both compact and non-compact modes for more coverage.
insights.lesson_learned: Stress tests near integer boundaries help catch overflow/edge-case bugs.

insights.title: Randomized concurrency stress test for StringBuilder
insights.problem: StringBuilder is mutable and needs robust testing under concurrent accesses (even though not thread-safe) to uncover racy behavior in implementation internals.
insights.root_cause: Low-level StringBuilder changes may interact poorly with concurrent access (test uses single SB across platform threads to stress race conditions).
insights.solution: Added StressSBTest which randomly invokes public StringBuilder instance methods across multiple platform threads for a duration while logging exceptions and stats.
insights.lesson_learned: While StringBuilder isn't thread-safe by contract, stress tests help find latent robustness issues in internal state transitions; use randomized invocation mapping for coverage.

insights.title: Adjust expected order of assertEquals arguments
insights.problem: Some tests compared expected vs actual with reversed order causing brittle messages; also added bug id.
insights.root_cause: Minor assertion ordering issues and test metadata updates.
insights.solution: Swapped assertEquals argument order in a couple of places and updated copyright.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep assertion argument ordering conventional (expected, actual) for clearer failures.

insights.title: Improve logging when default truststore provider is unspecified
insights.problem: When provider string was empty, logs showed blank provider, which is unclear.
insights.root_cause: The logging message printed storeProvider directly even when empty.
insights.solution: Log 'unspecified' when storeProvider.isEmpty().
insights.lesson_learned: Make diagnostic logging explicit for empty/unspecified config values to improve debuggability.

insights.title: Turn off cds logging to avoid lib/modules differences in cmp-baseline
insights.problem: cmp-baseline build failure due to diffs in lib/modules affected by CDS logging behavior producing differing artifacts.
insights.root_cause: Dump/Shared operations invoked without -Xlog:cds=off leading to non-deterministic differences.
insights.solution: Add -Xlog:cds=off to java invocations in classlist generation and shared archive dump steps.
insights.lesson_learned: Build tooling must control logging of subsystems that influence generated artifacts to ensure deterministic outputs for comparisons.

insights.title: Add macOS15 failures to Problem List
insights.problem: Some GUI tests fail on macOS15 and need to be listed as known problems to avoid CI noise.
insights.root_cause: Platform-specific behavior on macOS15 affecting AWT tests.
insights.solution: Add entries for MaximizedToMaximized, FileListBetweenJVMsTest and mark MissingDragExitEventTest for macosx-all.
insights.lesson_learned: Maintain platform-specific problem lists to keep CI stable while issues are investigated.

insights.title: Test fetches image via local file URL instead of remote
insights.problem: Test used network URL to fetch image which could cause timeouts and flakiness in headless environment.
insights.root_cause: Network access in tests can be unreliable or blocked, causing timeouts.
insights.solution: Use a local test resource file converted to URL (image.toURI().toURL()) and reorganize imports; ensure resource is accessed deterministically.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid external network dependencies in tests; use local resources to prevent timeouts and flakiness.

insights.title: Reduce memory consumption in BigInteger.pow()
insights.problem: BigInteger.pow() created intermediate BigInteger objects and used algorithms that allocated extra arrays unnecessarily for small cases.
insights.root_cause: Old code handled small/large cases with branching that required boxing into BigInteger and repeated allocations; also used multiprecision loops not optimized for unsigned long path.
insights.solution: Refactored pow to handle simple cases early: return ONE if exponent==0 or base==1, handle sign separately, factor out powersOfTwo, use unsigned long fast-path (unsignedLongPow) when scale fits in Long.SIZE, refactor repeated squaring loop to minimize temporaries and allocate result with new BigInteger(long mag, int signum) to avoid extra valueOf call, add overflow checks.
insights.lesson_learned: Special-case small/fit-in-word computations to avoid allocating full-precision representations; provide helper unsignedLongPow for repeated-squaring in long domain.

insights.title: Microbench for BigInteger.pow changes
insights.problem: Validate performance and memory improvements of new pow implementation across sizes and exponents.
insights.root_cause: Need objective data to ensure refactor improved memory/perf.
insights.solution: Added JMH benchmarks for different operand sizes and fixed/random exponents.
insights.lesson_learned: Benchmarks are important when optimizing core numeric routines.

insights.title: Use cp -R instead of cp -r for macOS compatibility
insights.problem: Copy command used -r; on macOS cp -R is the recommended recursive option and more compatible with copying bundles and symlinks.
insights.root_cause: Platform subtlety in cp semantics.
insights.solution: Switch to cp -R in helper's sudo and cp invocations.
insights.lesson_learned: Use platform-appropriate command-line flags in test helpers to avoid cross-unix differences.

insights.title: Do not follow symlinks and support symlinked content in app content tests
insights.problem: Test assumed copy of resource links would be treated like files; with NOFOLLOW_LINKS change, test needed to create and verify symbolic links.
insights.root_cause: Behavior changed to not follow symlinks, so test must create explicit symlinks and assert their presence.
insights.solution: Refactor test to support Resources/Links directories, create symlink test artifact, adjust detection and assertions (assertSymbolicLinkExists), and avoid following links during copy.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing API semantics regarding symlink handling, update tests to validate both content and link-preservation behavior.

insights.title: Use Long.hashCode for device/inode hashing
insights.problem: hashCode implementation used manual folding of long to int via shifts/xor; repetitive code.
insights.root_cause: Legacy style instead of using standard helper.
insights.solution: Use Long.hashCode(st_dev) + Long.hashCode(st_ino).
insights.lesson_learned: Use standard utilities (Long.hashCode) for consistent semantics and clarity.

insights.title: Use Long.hashCode for UnixFileKey.hashCode
insights.problem: Manual long folding replaced by Long.hashCode for clarity.
insights.root_cause: Same as FileKey.
insights.solution: Return Long.hashCode(st_dev) + Long.hashCode(st_ino).
insights.lesson_learned: Prefer built-in helpers for hashCode computations.

insights.title: Use Long.hashCode for UnixFileStore.hashCode
insights.problem: Manual folding of dev long used XOR with dir hash; updated for clarity/consistency.
insights.root_cause: Consistency improvement.
insights.solution: Use Long.hashCode(dev) ^ Arrays.hashCode(entry.dir()).
insights.lesson_learned: Consistent use of Long.hashCode across filesystem classes improves readability and reduces accidental mistakes.

insights.title: Reduce generated classes to avoid timeouts with AOTClassLinking and speed up verification
insights.problem: Test timed out when generating/processing too many synthetic classes while AOTClassLinking was enabled.
insights.root_cause: generate 100k classes was expensive for verification and archive steps; VerifyDependencies slowed test significantly.
insights.solution: Reduce top-level classes from 100->70 (70k classes) which still pushes CDS limits, and disable verification flags (VerifyBeforeExit, VerifyDependencies) to speed up test runs.
insights.lesson_learned: Stress tests must balance pushing limits and practical CI timeouts; tuning generator size combined with disabling costly verification can stabilize tests.

insights.title: Avoid NPE when tzdata was downgraded (ZoneInfo.getTimeZone may return null)
insights.problem: ZoneInfo.getTimeZone(id) may return null after tzdata downgrade, causing NPE when calling toZoneId().getRules().isFixedOffset().
insights.root_cause: Code assumed ZoneInfo.getTimeZone() always returns non-null.
insights.solution: Add helper isFixedOffset(id) that handles null return (treat as fixed-offset) and use it in deriveFallbackName/deriveFallbackNames.
insights.lesson_learned: Defensive checks are required when underlying data (tzdata) may be replaced/downgraded; avoid assumptions of non-null for lookups that can fail.

insights.title: Avoid IllegalStateException from nested/recursive formatting by preserving state
insights.problem: enter() threw IllegalStateException if nameSimplifier or whereClauses already set, which breaks in reentrant formatting scenarios introduced by recent changes.
insights.root_cause: Formatting became reentrant (format calling other formatting paths) and enter()/exit() were not robust to nested calls.
insights.solution: Refactored enter to accept Supplier<String> that installs temporary state and restores prior state in finally; replaced explicit enter/exit usage with enter(() -> { ... }).
insights.lesson_learned: When mutable formatter state may be used re-entrantly, prefer reentrant-safe patterns that snapshot/restore state in a try/finally rather than global set/clear paired calls.

insights.title: Re-entrant formatting regression test for RichDiagnosticFormatter
insights.problem: Compilation error paths can invoke formatting recursively and previously caused IllegalStateException.
insights.root_cause: Missing nested-state handling in formatter.
insights.solution: Added test that creates a scenario where formatting recurses (annotation/type use + missing class) and verifies compilation fails but does not crash.
insights.lesson_learned: Add regression tests for reentrant formatting and error paths that previously triggered crashes.

insights.title: Robustly wait for thread to reach blocking point before checking deadlock
insights.problem: Test sometimes probed thread state before the thread reached the synchronized block, causing false negatives.
insights.root_cause: Using only getState()==BLOCKED can race with thread not having entered the synchronized region yet.
insights.solution: Add AtomicBoolean flags (reached1/reached2) set by threads after they reach the barrier and before attempting the second synchronization, and wait on both flag==true and state==BLOCKED via awaitTrueAndBlocked.
insights.lesson_learned: When testing thread deadlocks, ensure the test waits for a per-thread ready signal before asserting blocked state to avoid races.

insights.title: Cleanup interp_only_mode handling and use boolean setters
insights.problem: interp_only_mode was being manipulated as integer increment/decrement and mixing with booleans caused unclear semantics; mixing of 0/1 and increments led to subtle bugs.
insights.root_cause: Code used increment/decrement semantics (counting) but interpreter checks only need boolean state; saved state used int and sometimes assigned 0/1 inconsistently.
insights.solution: Replace increment/decrement with set_interp_only_mode(true/false) and use boolean saved flag; assert entering interp-only mode isn't already active; adjust saved restoration semantics.
insights.lesson_learned: Prefer boolean setters for binary state rather than integer counters unless counting is required. Make invariants explicit with asserts.

insights.title: Save interp_only_mode as boolean
insights.problem: Saved interp_only_mode field used int before; inconsistent with new boolean semantics.
insights.root_cause: Migration from int counters to boolean flags required field repositioning.
insights.solution: Changed _saved_interp_only_mode type to bool and moved declaration for clear semantics; updated is_interp_only_mode() to use bool.
insights.lesson_learned: When changing type semantics (int counter->bool flag), keep field location/ordering clear and adapt all accessors.

insights.title: Use boolean accessors when saving/restoring interp_only_mode
insights.problem: Unbind/bind logic used int get/set; migrated to boolean semantics and ensure proper saved semantics when unmounted.
insights.root_cause: Keeping integer semantics while rest of code switched to boolean produced confusing assignments.
insights.solution: Assign state->_saved_interp_only_mode = thread->is_interp_only_mode(); and set thread->set_interp_only_mode(...bool...); simplified unmount path.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep unbind/bind symmetric and use semantic boolean names to avoid off-by-one counting errors.

insights.title: Make _interp_only_mode an int but provide boolean setter/getter interface
insights.problem: Interpreter expects an int storage for _interp_only_mode field because it is read by interpreter in assembly; code moved to boolean semantics but storage must remain int for interpreter ABI.
insights.root_cause: Interpreter assembly code relies on integer field layout and offset; changing to bool storage could break ABI.
insights.solution: Keep int _interp_only_mode field but provide set_interp_only_mode(bool) that sets 0/1, and is_interp_only_mode() returns (_interp_only_mode!=0). Removed increment/decrement/getters to avoid misuse.
insights.lesson_learned: When storage layout is part of ABI with interpreter/native code, keep the underlying representation compatible but provide safer high-level accessors.
